XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Y Cynnig Gofal Plant
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: The Childcare Offer

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 3. Beth mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei wneud i sicrhau bod ei chynnig gofal plant yn hyblyg ac yn diwallu anghenion rhieni? OQ64647
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 3. What is the Welsh Government doing to ensure that its childcare offer is flexible and meets the needs of parents? OQ64647

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Funded childcare must be flexible for families and deliverable for providers. We're working with local authorities and registered providers to expand provision sustainably and move to a simpler system that's easier for parents to navigate. As we introduce our universal childcare offer, we will ensure that it will enable longer and more flexible sessions.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae'n rhaid i ofal plant a ariennir fod yn hyblyg i deuluoedd ac yn gyflawnadwy i ddarparwyr. Rydyn ni'n gweithio gydag awdurdodau lleol a darparwyr cofrestredig i ehangu'r ddarpariaeth yn gynaliadwy a symud i system symlach sy'n haws i rieni ei llywio. Wrth i ni gyflwyno ein cynnig gofal plant cyffredinol, byddwn ni'n sicrhau y bydd yn galluogi sesiynau hirach a mwy hyblyg.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Brif Weinidog. I'd like to give an example of how the current system isn't flexible for parents. One nursery I know of in Cardiff can only provide Flying Start provision for 2.5 hours a day for the children who are eligible, but, meanwhile, the same nursery group in Newport can provide Flying Start in blocks so that parents can return to work part-time and use their Flying Start hours all in a couple of days. Parents in Cardiff aren't offered the same opportunities. Currently, funded childcare provision is too fragmented. It's a postcode lottery between local authorities and even different sides of the street. Too many who need it cannot access it.

Labour are complaining about a universal childcare offer. We've heard it again today—Labour complaining about universal childcare. The party of Aneurin Bevan and universal healthcare is complaining about universalism. They've lost touch with their roots. Meanwhile, Reform in England are closing publicly funded nurseries. So, does the First Minister agree with me that the universality of this childcare offer is key, so that parents can get back to work and not a single child slips through that gap in provision?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Hoffwn roi enghraifft o sut nad yw'r system bresennol yn hyblyg i rieni. Dim ond am 2.5 awr y dydd y gall un feithrinfa rwy'n gwybod amdani yng Nghaerdydd ddarparu darpariaeth Dechrau'n Deg i'r plant sy'n gymwys, ond, yn y cyfamser, gall yr un grŵp meithrin yng Nghasnewydd ddarparu Dechrau'n Deg mewn blociau fel y gall rhieni ddychwelyd i'r gwaith yn rhan-amser a defnyddio eu horiau Dechrau'n Deg i gyd mewn cwpl o ddiwrnodau. Dydy rhieni yng Nghaerdydd ddim yn cael cynnig yr un cyfleoedd. Ar hyn o bryd, mae darpariaeth gofal plant wedi'i hariannu yn rhy dameidiog. Mae'n loteri cod post rhwng awdurdodau lleol a hyd yn oed gwahanol ochrau i'r stryd. Mae gormod o bobl sydd ei hangen yn methu cael mynediad iddi.

Mae Llafur yn cwyno am gynnig gofal plant cyffredinol. Rydyn ni wedi ei glywed eto heddiw—Llafur yn cwyno am ofal plant cyffredinol. Mae plaid Aneurin Bevan a gofal iechyd cyffredinol yn cwyno am gyffredinoliaeth. Maen nhw wedi colli cysylltiad â'u gwreiddiau. Yn y cyfamser, mae Reform yn Lloegr yn cau meithrinfeydd sy'n cael eu hariannu'n gyhoeddus. Felly, a yw'r Prif Weinidog yn cytuno â mi fod cyffredinolrwydd y cynnig gofal plant hwn yn allweddol, fel bod rhieni y gallu mynd yn ôl i'r gwaith ac nad oes yr un plentyn yn llithro trwy'r bwlch hwnnw yn y ddarpariaeth?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
That universality is very, very important and, as we've touched on already today, it is a broader principle that we should value.

On flexibility, as we introduce a radical, an ambitious, new national childcare offer, we're working to create a simpler, more streamlined system that gives parents more flexibility and easier access to funded childcare across Wales. Universal provision, of course, supports every child to get the best start in life, and thousands of low-earning families who've previously been locked out of any childcare or early years support will benefit as a result of our policy. Current guidance allows childcare sessions to be combined. We know this flexibility is interpreted and applied differently, and we are working to, as we roll out the childcare offer, partner with local authorities and others to make sure that that consistency does become the norm across the board.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae'r cyffredinolrwydd hwnnw'n bwysig iawn, iawn ac, fel rydyn ni wedi'i grybwyll eisoes heddiw, mae'n egwyddor ehangach y dylem ei gwerthfawrogi.

O ran hyblygrwydd, wrth i ni gyflwyno cynnig gofal plant cenedlaethol newydd radical, uchelgeisiol, rydyn ni'n gweithio i greu system symlach sy'n rhoi mwy o hyblygrwydd i rieni a mynediad haws at ofal plant a ariennir ledled Cymru. Mae darpariaeth gyffredinol, wrth gwrs, yn cefnogi pob plentyn i gael y dechrau gorau mewn bywyd, a bydd miloedd o deuluoedd ar gyflogau isel sydd wedi'u cloi allan o unrhyw ofal plant neu gymorth blynyddoedd cynnar yn flaenorol yn elwa o ganlyniad i'n polisi. Mae'r canllawiau cyfredol yn caniatáu i sesiynau gofal plant gael eu cyfuno. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod yr hyblygrwydd hwn yn cael ei ddehongli a'i gymhwyso'n wahanol, ac wrth i ni gyflwyno'r cynnig gofal plant, rydyn ni'n gweithio i bartneru ag awdurdodau lleol ac eraill i sicrhau bod y cysondeb hwnnw'n dod yn beth arferol yn gyffredinol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prif Weinidog, last week your Deputy First Minister told me that childcare must be flexible for families and deliverable for providers. Yet, when I asked what this expanded offer will actually cost, she told me that the figures will only become clear in the forthcoming draft budget. But flexibility has a price tag. Longer hours, greater capacity, rural provision and the workforce to deliver it cannot be paid for with aspiration. So, how can your Government promise parents a flexible childcare offer when it still cannot tell them or this Senedd what the fully modelled policy will cost? Surely you cost the flexibility before you promise it, rather than promise it first and work out the bill afterwards. Because however flexible the promise, First Minister, the budget remains stubbornly inflexible. Eventually, the numbers will have to add up. So, please reassure us that Welsh parents will not be left quite as baffled by your childcare maths as your Deputy First Minister apparently was by mine.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, yr wythnos diwethaf fe ddywedodd eich Dirprwy Brif Weinidog wrthyf fod yn rhaid i ofal plant fod yn hyblyg i deuluoedd ac yn gyflawnadwy i ddarparwyr. Eto, pan ofynnais i beth fydd y cynnig estynedig hwn yn ei gostio mewn gwirionedd, fe ddywedodd wrthyf mai dim ond yn y gyllideb ddrafft sydd ar ddod y bydd y ffigurau'n dod yn glir. Ond mae yna gostau ynghlwm wrth hyblygrwydd. Ni ellir talu am oriau hirach, mwy o gapasiti, darpariaeth wledig a'r gweithlu i'w gyflawni gyda dyhead. Felly, sut all eich Llywodraeth addo cynnig gofal plant hyblyg i rieni pan nad yw'n gallu dweud wrthyn nhw na'r Senedd hon o hyd beth fydd y polisi wedi'i fodelu'n llawn yn ei gostio? Does bosib eich bod chi'n pennu cost yr hyblygrwydd cyn i chi ei addo, yn hytrach na'i addo yn gyntaf a gweithio'r bil allan wedyn. Oherwydd ni waeth pa mor hyblyg yw'r addewid, Brif Weinidog, mae'r gyllideb yn parhau i fod yn ystyfnig o anhyblyg. Yn y pen draw, bydd yn rhaid i'r rhifau adio i fyny. Felly, plîs a wnewch chi ein sicrhau ni na fydd rhieni yng Nghymru yn cael eu drysu cymaint gan eich mathemateg gofal plant ag y cafodd eich Dirprwy Brif Weinidog, yn ôl pob golwg, gan fy mathemateg i.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Well, I fundamentally disagree with that take from the Member. We've made it clear. In fact, we have put the money in for the first phase, which is the rolling out of the 12.5 hours in every part of Wales within this first financial year. It's £55 million, and that is—. Well, that's happening. The money has gone. It's £55 million. Working towards the end of roll-out in a Government term, you're talking about a significant sum, £300 million to £400 million, depending on uptake and so on. There are lots of different factors. But this was meant to be, and is being, done in a phased way, which is the only way that it can be done. It's not just because of the money; one of the big challenges that we are facing, and dealing with, is workforce. We visited a nursery in Rhyl last week, and there's real excitement about how to bring more young people into the profession, which we will need to do in significant numbers to roll out this childcare offer, which will transform lives.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wel, rwy'n anghytuno'n llwyr â'r safbwynt hwnnw gan yr Aelod. Rydyn ni wedi ei wneud yn glir. Yn wir, rydyn ni wedi rhoi'r arian i mewn ar gyfer y cam cyntaf, sef cyflwyno'r 12.5 awr ym mhob rhan o Gymru o fewn y flwyddyn ariannol gyntaf hon. Mae'n £55 miliwn, ac mae hynny—. Wel, mae hynny'n digwydd. Mae'r arian wedi mynd. Mae'n £55 miliwn. Wrth weithio tuag at orffen y gwaith cyflwyno mewn tymor y Llywodraeth, rydych chi'n sôn am swm sylweddol, £300 miliwn i £400 miliwn, yn dibynnu ar y defnydd ac yn y blaen. Mae yna lawer o wahanol ffactorau. Ond roedd hyn i fod i gael ei wneud, ac mae'n cael ei wneud, mewn ffordd raddol, sef yr unig ffordd y gellir ei wneud. Nid dim ond oherwydd yr arian; un o'r heriau mawr rydyn ni'n ei hwynebu, ac rydyn ni'n delio â hi, yw'r gweithlu. Fe wnaethon ni ymweld â meithrinfa yn y Rhyl yr wythnos diwethaf, ac mae yna gyffro go iawn ynglŷn â sut i ddod â mwy o bobl ifanc i'r proffesiwn, y bydd angen i ni ei wneud mewn niferoedd sylweddol i gyflwyno'r cynnig gofal plant hwn, a fydd yn trawsnewid bywydau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, we've heard from Kiera Marshall very clearly that access to childcare is heavily dependent on where you live; Flying Start is a great example. So, you are declaring—your Government says—that its new offer will be flexible and responsive to parents' needs, which is great, but is that really going to take effect? We talked about rural-proofing earlier. Will rural-proofing enable this to happen in our rural communities? Can we truly see a levelling-up and a universality, as you said, of childcare in those most hard-to-reach areas like I represent?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rydyn ni wedi clywed gan Kiera Marshall yn glir iawn bod mynediad at ofal plant yn dibynnu'n fawr ar ble rydych chi'n byw; mae Dechrau'n Deg yn enghraifft wych. Felly, rydych chi'n datgan—mae eich Llywodraeth yn dweud—y bydd ei chynnig newydd yn hyblyg ac yn ymatebol i anghenion rhieni, sy'n wych, ond a yw hynny'n mynd i gael effaith? Fe wnaethon ni siarad am brawfesur gwledig yn gynharach. A fydd prawfesur gwledig yn galluogi hyn i ddigwydd yn ein cymunedau gwledig? Allwn ni weld lefelu i fyny go iawn a chyffredinoldeb, fel y dywedsoch chi, o ran gofal plant yn yr ardaloedd hynny sydd anoddaf eu cyrraedd fel yr wyf i'n eu cynrychioli?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As you mentioned rural-proofing and Flying Start, I'll maybe bring those two together. Flying Start has done a great job in helping families who are struggling to make ends meet in some parts of Wales. I know of parts in my own constituency, and many others will have their own experiences of families who are outside Flying Start areas, in rural areas who are unable to get that kind of support. What we're doing in building on Flying Start, not cutting it, is making sure that we are expanding this universally to all people, universally to all areas, because we have identified this as something that could be the underpinnings of education, of job opportunities and tackling poverty. We're not setting simple targets for ourselves here. We're stretching ourselves because we think it's important, and rurality is very much a part of the mix.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gan eich bod chi wedi sôn am brawfesur gwledig a Dechrau'n Deg, efallai y gwnaf i ddod â'r ddau at ei gilydd. Mae Dechrau'n Deg wedi gwneud gwaith gwych yn helpu teuluoedd sy'n ei chael hi'n anodd cael dau ben llinyn ynghyd mewn rhai rhannau o Gymru. Rwy'n gwybod am rannau o fy etholaeth fy hun, a bydd gan lawer o bobl eraill eu profiadau eu hunain o deuluoedd sydd y tu allan i ardaloedd Dechrau'n Deg, mewn ardaloedd gwledig nad ydynt yn gallu cael y math hwnnw o gymorth. Yr hyn rydyn ni'n ei wneud wrth adeiladu ar Dechrau'n Deg, nid ei dorri, yw gwneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n ehangu hyn yn gyffredinol i bawb, yn gyffredinol i bob ardal, oherwydd rydyn ni wedi nodi bod hyn yn rhywbeth a allai fod yn sail i addysg, i gyfleoedd gwaith ac i fynd i'r afael â thlodi. Dydyn ni ddim yn gosod targedau syml i ni ein hunain yn y fan yma. Rydyn ni'n ymestyn ein hunain oherwydd rydyn ni'n meddwl ei fod yn bwysig, ac mae gwledigrwydd yn sicr yn rhan o'r gymysgedd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Chwaraeon Proffesiynol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Professional Sport

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 4. Pa asesiad y mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi'i wneud o effaith chwaraeon proffesiynol ar economi Cymru? OQ64617
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 4. What assessment has the First Minister made of the impact of professional sport on the Welsh economy? OQ64617

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Professional sport makes a significant contribution to the Welsh economy. It brings visitors into our communities, supports local businesses, creates jobs and showcases Wales to a global audience, at home and abroad. I'll take the opportunity to congratulate Elfyn Evans again on waving the flag in Sardinia on Sunday. But, from the Tour de France Grand Départ to Euro 2028, Wales has shown that it is able to attract world-class sporting events. What we need to do always is make sure that those events leave a lasting legacy for communities across Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae chwaraeon proffesiynol yn gwneud cyfraniad sylweddol i economi Cymru. Mae'n dod ag ymwelwyr i'n cymunedau, yn cefnogi busnesau lleol, yn creu swyddi ac yn arddangos Cymru i gynulleidfa fyd-eang, gartref a thramor. Fe wnaf i achub ar y cyfle i longyfarch Elfyn Evans eto ar chwifio'r faner yn Sardinia ddydd Sul. Ond, o'r Tour de France Grand Départ i Euro 2028, mae Cymru wedi dangos ei bod yn gallu denu digwyddiadau chwaraeon o'r radd flaenaf. Yr hyn y mae angen i ni ei wneud bob amser yw sicrhau bod y digwyddiadau hynny'n gadael gwaddol parhaol i gymunedau ledled Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, First Minister. I agree with you. Sport can have a huge impact on the economy, as we've seen in places like Swansea—when they made the Premier League, tens of millions of pounds put into the economy there—and here in Cardiff, when they were a part of the Premier League. We've seen success with Wrexham now, having an impact on their economy, in Newport, and with other sports as well, like when the Ryder Cup came to Wales, and we've seen it when the wrestling was in Cardiff. But what future plans has the Welsh Government got to encourage more of these large-scale events that can bring better, high-paying jobs during those periods and that can boost our hospitality industry, but not only to current areas that are seeing that—how about if we can attract more of these large-scale events to other parts of Wales yet to be showcased around the world?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch, Brif Weinidog. Rwy'n cytuno â chi. Gall chwaraeon gael effaith enfawr ar yr economi, fel rydyn ni wedi'i weld mewn llefydd fel Abertawe—pan wnaethon nhw gyrraedd yr Uwch Gynghrair, degau o filiynau o bunnoedd yn cael eu rhoi i'r economi yno—ac yma yng Nghaerdydd, pan oedden nhw'n rhan o'r Uwch Gynghrair. Rydyn ni wedi gweld llwyddiant gyda Wrecsam nawr, yn cael effaith ar eu heconomi, yng Nghasnewydd, a chyda chwaraeon eraill hefyd, fel pan ddaeth Cwpan Ryder i Gymru, ac rydyn ni wedi ei weld pan oedd y reslo yng Nghaerdydd. Ond pa gynlluniau sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer y dyfodol i gymell mwy o'r digwyddiadau mawr hyn a all ddod â swyddi gwell sy'n talu'n dda yn ystod y cyfnodau hynny ac a all roi hwb i'n diwydiant lletygarwch, ond nid dim ond i'r ardaloedd sy'n gweld hynny nawr—tybed a allem ddenu mwy o'r digwyddiadau mawr hyn i rannau eraill o Gymru sydd heb gael eu harddangos o amgylch y byd eto?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I believe in the principle of seeing what we can do to attract events. We've got the Women's Champions League final as well coming to Cardiff. It's not always Government that delivers them. Government can be a facilitator. Government can be a conduit for making them happen. We want to work with others when they see opportunities to bring global sporting events to Wales. Like having overseas offices, it is all part of that—[Interruption.] It is all part of that work of raising Wales's profile on the world stage, and the benefits that flow from that are multiple. This soft diplomacy, plus the hard numbers of where we can attract, through sporting events, international inward investment, is something that we should embrace, all of us here, because Wales can only win from this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu yn yr egwyddor o weld beth allwn ni ei wneud i ddenu digwyddiadau. Mae gennym ni rownd derfynol Cynghrair Pencampwyr y Merched hefyd yn dod i Gaerdydd. Nid y Llywodraeth sy'n eu cyflawni bob amser. Gall y Llywodraeth fod yn hwylusydd. Gall y Llywodraeth fod yn gyfrwng i wneud iddyn nhw ddigwydd. Rydyn ni eisiau gweithio gydag eraill pan fyddan nhw'n gweld cyfleoedd i ddod â digwyddiadau chwaraeon byd-eang i Gymru. Fel cael swyddfeydd tramor, mae'r cyfan yn rhan o'r—[Torri ar draws.] Mae'r cyfan yn rhan o'r gwaith hwnnw o godi proffil Cymru ar y llwyfan rhyngwladol, ac mae cymaint o fanteision yn deillio o hynny. Mae'r ddiplomyddiaeth feddal hon, ynghyd â'r ffigurau manwl o ran ble y gallwn ni ddenu, trwy ddigwyddiadau chwaraeon, fewnfuddsoddiad rhyngwladol, yn rhywbeth y dylem ei gofleidio, pob un ohonom ni yma, oherwydd dim ond ennill y gall Cymru ei gwneud o hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Prif Weinidog, I'd like to focus on the people behind the sports. Every sporting journey is built on dedication, discipline and enormous personal sacrifice, whether or not an athlete ultimately reaches the highest level of success, or even achieves financial success. Being an elite athlete is a unique way of life because, for many, their lives are structured around training, competition, travel, performance targets, coaches and team mates, often from a very young age. Education and career opportunities can be shaped around that commitment too, making the transition out of sport particularly challenging. While just a small number go on to gain financial security, many athletes make significant sacrifices without that sustainable living that comes afterwards. Yet many do leave sport with valuable skills in leadership, resilience, discipline, teamwork and performing under pressure, skills that can only benefit the wider Welsh economy and inspire future generations. So, Prif Weinidog, what support is the Welsh Government providing to support athletes transitioning into sustainable careers when they leave professional sport?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, hoffwn ganolbwyntio ar y bobl y tu ôl i'r chwaraeon. Mae pob taith chwaraeon wedi'i hadeiladu ar ymroddiad, disgyblaeth ac aberth personol enfawr, p'un a fydd athletwr yn cyrraedd y lefel uchaf o lwyddiant yn y pen draw ai peidio, neu hyd yn oed yn cael llwyddiant ariannol. Mae bod yn athletwr elitaidd yn ffordd unigryw o fyw oherwydd, i lawer, mae eu bywydau wedi'u strwythuro o amgylch hyfforddiant, cystadleuaeth, teithio, targedau perfformiad, hyfforddwyr a chyd-chwaraewyr, yn aml o oedran ifanc iawn. Gall addysg a chyfleoedd gyrfa gael eu siapio o amgylch yr ymrwymiad hwnnw hefyd, gan wneud y pontio allan o chwaraeon yn arbennig o heriol. Er mai dim ond nifer bach sy'n mynd ymlaen i sicrhau diogelwch ariannol, mae llawer o athletwyr yn gwneud aberth sylweddol heb y bywyd cynaliadwy hwnnw sy'n dod wedyn. Ond mae llawer yn gadael chwaraeon gyda sgiliau gwerthfawr mewn arweinyddiaeth, gwydnwch, disgyblaeth, gwaith tîm a pherfformio dan bwysau, sgiliau a all ond fod o fudd i economi ehangach Cymru ac ysbrydoli cenedlaethau'r dyfodol. Felly, Brif Weinidog, pa gymorth y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn ei roi i gefnogi athletwyr sy'n symud i yrfaoedd cynaliadwy ar ôl gadael chwaraeon proffesiynol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Llywydd, I know the Member speaks from her own experience working in sports governance before being elected here. But I'd say that, through our investment as a Government in elite sports, we support partners, including Sport Wales and other governing bodies, to help athletes prepare for life beyond sport, through education, through training and through career development opportunities. There are so many of them—Welsh Athletics, Swim Wales, Hoci Cymru—they all support athletes to gain coaching, officiating and leadership qualifications alongside their sporting careers. Many former elite athletes go on to become coaches, performance managers, board members and ambassadors within their sports. The Football Association of Wales is particularly good at being a centre of excellence for preparing the coaches of the future, not just for Wales, but for other nations too. And developing that pipeline is key, I think, to ensuring that the skills, the experience and the inspiration gained through representing Wales or competing in elite sports continue to benefit our economy, our communities and our sporting success in future.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Lywydd, rwy'n gwybod bod yr Aelod yn siarad o'i phrofiad ei hun o weithio ym maes llywodraethu chwaraeon cyn cael ei hethol yma. Ond byddwn i'n dweud, trwy ein buddsoddiad fel Llywodraeth mewn chwaraeon elitaidd, ein bod ni'n cefnogi partneriaid, gan gynnwys Chwaraeon Cymru a chyrff llywodraethu eraill, i helpu athletwyr i baratoi ar gyfer bywyd y tu hwnt i chwaraeon, trwy addysg, trwy hyfforddiant a thrwy gyfleoedd datblygu gyrfa. Mae cynifer ohonyn nhw—Athletau Cymru, Nofio Cymru, Hoci Cymru—maen nhw i gyd yn cefnogi athletwyr i ennill cymwysterau hyfforddi, gweinyddu ac arwain ochr yn ochr â'u gyrfaoedd chwaraeon. Mae llawer o gyn-athletwyr elitaidd yn mynd ymlaen i fod yn hyfforddwyr, rheolwyr perfformiad, aelodau bwrdd a llysgenhadon yn eu campau. Mae Cymdeithas Bêl-droed Cymru yn arbennig o dda am fod yn ganolfan ragoriaeth ar gyfer paratoi hyfforddwyr y dyfodol, nid yn unig i Gymru, ond i wledydd eraill hefyd. Ac mae datblygu'r biblinell honno yn allweddol, rwy'n credu, i sicrhau bod y sgiliau, y profiad a'r ysbrydoliaeth a gafwyd trwy gynrychioli Cymru neu gystadlu mewn chwaraeon elitaidd yn parhau i fod o fudd i'n heconomi, i'n cymunedau ac i'n llwyddiant ym maes chwaraeon yn y dyfodol.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'm a Swansea City Association Football Club supporter and I remember the effect that playing in the premiership, winning the league cup and qualifying in Europe had on the image of Swansea. I drove down Mumbles Road one Saturday morning and a huge crowd of Chelsea supporters were walking towards the city centre. They had stayed in Swansea overnight, paid for accommodation, food and drink, helping our economy. The Ospreys, when they have European games against French and English opponents, also generate a substantial number of overnight supporters, with the same effect. Does the First Minister agree with me that the success of professional sport is beneficial for our economy, and that Swansea needs Swansea City back in the premiership and a successful Ospreys team? [Laughter.]
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n cefnogi Clwb Pêl-droed Dinas Abertawe ac rwy'n cofio'r effaith a gafodd chwarae yn yr uwch gynghrair, ennill cwpan y gynghrair a sicrhau lle yn Ewrop ar ddelwedd Abertawe. Fe wnes i yrru i lawr Heol y Mwmbwls un bore Sadwrn ac roedd torf enfawr o gefnogwyr Chelsea yn cerdded tuag at ganol y ddinas. Roedden nhw wedi aros yn Abertawe dros nos, wedi talu am lety, bwyd a diod, gan helpu ein heconomi. Mae'r Gweilch, pan maen nhw'n chwarae gemau Ewropeaidd yn erbyn gwrthwynebwyr o Ffrainc a Lloegr, hefyd yn denu nifer sylweddol o gefnogwyr dros nos, gyda'r un effaith. Ydy'r Prif Weinidog yn cytuno â mi bod llwyddiant chwaraeon proffesiynol yn fuddiol i'n heconomi, a bod Abertawe angen Dinas Abertawe yn ôl yn yr uwch gynghrair a llwyddiant i dîm y Gweilch? [Chwerthin.]

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Right then, I'm going to have to be careful here. 'Yes' is the answer to the question. I have no doubt that professional sporting events, which happen week in, week out, of course, through professional sport in football and rugby, can bring huge, huge benefits, and supporting those hospitality sectors that support those coming to support their teams, that's something that we should encourage always.

Do I want to see Swansea City being promoted to the premier league? Absolutely, yes. As a Cardiff City Football Club fan, they can only go up if we go up as well. And let's make it Wrexham also. Because, genuinely, I think the success of Welsh football currently—. I see Jayne Bryant looking at me here—I wish Newport all the very, very best too, and all league of Wales teams. [Laughter.] But, no, I think the success of our football teams is something that we can all celebrate, whichever colour we individually choose to wear.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Iawn te, rwy'n mynd i orfod bod yn ofalus yn y fan yma. 'Ydw' yw'r ateb i'r cwestiwn. Does gen i ddim amheuaeth bod digwyddiadau chwaraeon proffesiynol, sy'n digwydd wythnos ar ôl wythnos, wrth gwrs, trwy chwaraeon proffesiynol mewn pêl-droed a rygbi, yn gallu dod â manteision enfawr, enfawr, ac mae cefnogi'r sectorau lletygarwch hynny sy'n cynnal y rhai sy'n dod i gefnogi eu timau, mae hynny'n rhywbeth y dylem ei annog bob amser.

Ydw i eisiau gweld Dinas Abertawe yn cael ei dyrchafu i'r uwch gynghrair? Ydw, wrth gwrs. Fel cefnogwr Clwb Pêl-droed Dinas Caerdydd, gallan nhw ond mynd i fyny os gallwn ni fynd i fyny hefyd. A gadewch i ni weld Wrecsam yno hefyd. Oherwydd rwyf wir yn credu bod llwyddiant pêl-droed Cymru ar hyn o bryd—. Rwy'n gweld Jayne Bryant yn edrych arna' i yn y fan yma—rwy'n dymuno'r gorau i Gasnewydd hefyd, a holl dimau cynghrair Cymru. [Chwerthin.] Ond, na, rwy'n credu bod llwyddiant ein timau pêl-droed yn rhywbeth y gallwn ni i gyd ei ddathlu, pa liw bynnag rydyn ni'n dewis ei wisgo.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
First Minister, as you said, professional sport plays an important role in supporting local economies by creating jobs and generating investment in our communities. One good example is the expansion of the Novira Cymru Premier football league to 16 teams, with new branding, improved broadcasting and a stronger media presence, which has raised the profile and visibility of the league, which is indeed very welcome.

Now, this season, Haverfordwest County Association Football Club has adopted a hybrid model, combining full-time professional players with part-time players. The aim is to provide a pathway for local talent into senior football, while also further improving the club's competitiveness, building on its recent qualification for European competition, which has happened twice in recent years. So, in light of the economic impact that clubs can have on their communities, what further steps can the Welsh Government take to promote the Novira Cymru Premier football league and the clubs that actually compete in it, particularly in developing home-grown talent, strengthening their commercial profile and helping more Welsh clubs compete successfully on the European stage?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Brif Weinidog, fel y dywedsoch chi, mae chwaraeon proffesiynol yn chwarae rôl bwysig wrth gefnogi economïau lleol trwy greu swyddi a chynhyrchu buddsoddiad yn ein cymunedau. Un enghraifft dda yw ehangu Uwch Gynghrair Bêl-droed Novira Cymru i 16 o dimau, gyda brandio newydd, gwell darlledu a phresenoldeb cryfach yn y cyfryngau, sydd wedi codi proffil a gwelededd y gynghrair, sydd i'w groesawu'n fawr.

Nawr, y tymor hwn, mae Clwb Pêl-droed Sir Hwlffordd wedi mabwysiadu model hybrid, gan gyfuno chwaraewyr proffesiynol llawn amser gyda chwaraewyr rhan-amser. Y nod yw darparu llwybr i dalent leol i mewn i bêl-droed hŷn a gwella cystadleurwydd y clwb ymhellach hefyd, gan adeiladu ar ei lwyddiant diweddar yn sicrhau lle mewn cystadleuaeth Ewropeaidd, sydd wedi digwydd ddwywaith yn ystod y blynyddoedd diwethaf. Felly, yng ngoleuni'r effaith economaidd y gall clybiau ei chael ar eu cymunedau, pa gamau pellach y gall Llywodraeth Cymru eu cymryd i hyrwyddo Uwch Gynghrair Bêl-droed Novira Cymru a'r clybiau sy'n cystadlu ynddi, yn enwedig wrth ddatblygu talent o Gymru, cryfhau eu proffil masnachol a helpu mwy o glybiau Cymru i gystadlu'n llwyddiannus ar y llwyfan Ewropeaidd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Llywydd, I hope you've built lots of time into this, because everybody wants to name their local football team now, I think. But I wish Haverfordwest well.

I'm quite excited about premier football in Wales. Currently, there's been a lot of investment and there seems to be a real vibrancy around football at its highest level in Wales. I congratulate the work that the Football Association of Wales are doing. We engage with the Football Association of Wales in many different ways in supporting grass-roots sport, and we are happy to engage in any way that could see the Welsh Government supporting and facilitating the kind of investment that I know the FAW are determined to bring into Welsh football.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Lywydd, rwy'n gobeithio eich bod chi wedi neilltuo llawer o amser i hyn, oherwydd mae pawb eisiau enwi eu tîm pêl-droed lleol nawr, rwy'n meddwl. Ond rwy'n dymuno'n dda i Hwlffordd.

Rwy'n eithaf cyffrous am bêl-droed uwch gynghrair yng Nghymru. Ar hyn o bryd, mae llawer o fuddsoddiad wedi bod ac mae'n ymddangos bod bywiogrwydd go iawn o amgylch pêl-droed ar ei lefel uchaf yng Nghymru. Hoffwn longyfarch y gwaith y mae Cymdeithas Bêl-droed Cymru yn ei wneud. Rydyn ni'n ymgysylltu â Chymdeithas Bêl-droed Cymru mewn sawl ffordd wahanol i gefnogi chwaraeon ar lawr gwlad, ac rydyn ni'n hapus i ymgysylltu mewn unrhyw ffordd a allai weld Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi ac yn hwyluso'r math o fuddsoddiad rwy'n gwybod y mae'r Gymdeithas Bêl-droed yn benderfynol o'i sicrhau i bêl-droed yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: NHS Care

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 5. Pa gynnydd y mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi'i wneud o ran gwella mynediad amserol at ofal y GIG? OQ64675
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 5. What progress has the First Minister made on improving timely access to NHS care? OQ64675

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Our programme for government commits us to cutting waiting lists and building a health and care service fit for the future. Backed by £145 million of additional investment, we're taking immediate action to reduce waits for diagnosis and treatment, while accelerating the wider transformation of services, with a stronger focus on prevention, care closer to home and the needs of individuals and communities.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni'n ein hymrwymo i dorri rhestrau aros ac adeiladu gwasanaeth iechyd a gofal sy'n addas i'r dyfodol. Gyda chefnogaeth £145 miliwn o fuddsoddiad ychwanegol, rydym ni'n cymryd camau ar unwaith i fyrhau arosiadau am ddiagnosis a thriniaethau, wrth gyflymu trawsnewidiad gwasanaethau yn fwy eang, gan ganolbwyntio yn fwy ar atal, gofal yn nes at y cartref ac anghenion unigolion a chymunedau.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: First Minister, I'm sure you'll agree with me that when it comes to dentistry, it's important to drill into the data. Recent data shows that only 40 per cent of people were treated under an NHS dentist, a 40 per cent drop since 2020. It is very difficult for anybody now to access NHS dental treatment. Your own health Minister admitted in a committee recently that he faces a 60-mile round trip to see his dentist. When the flawed new dental contract came into force on 1 April, five practices in my area of Monmouthshire Torfaen stopped providing NHS care. Access to NHS dentists is absolutely vital, otherwise Wales will face more dental problems further down the road. What are you going to do about it, First Minister? Will you finally involve practising dentists to try and help solve this problem? The lack of accessibility to NHS dentists is now out of control.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Brif Weinidog, rwy'n siŵr y byddech chi'n cytuno â mi o ran deintyddiaeth, mae hi'n bwysig drilio i mewn i'r data. Mae data diweddar yn dangos mai dim ond 40 y cant o bobl gafodd eu trin dan ofal deintydd GIG, gostyngiad o 40 y cant ers 2020. Mae hi'n anodd iawn i unrhyw un gael triniaeth ddeintyddol yn y GIG nawr. Roedd eich Gweinidog iechyd chi eich hun yn cyfaddef mewn pwyllgor diweddar ei fod ef yn wynebu taith gron o 60 milltir er mwyn gweld ei ddeintydd. Pan ddaeth y contract deintyddol newydd diffygiol i rym ar 1 Ebrill, rhoddodd pum practis yn fy ardal i yn Sir Fynwy Torfaen y gorau i ddarparu gofal GIG. Mae argaeledd deintyddion GIG yn gwbl hanfodol, fel arall fe fydd Cymru yn wynebu mwy o broblemau deintyddol yn y dyfodol Beth ydych chi am ei wneud ynglŷn â'r mater, Brif Weinidog? A wnewch chi o'r diwedd gynnwys deintyddion sy'n ymarfer wrth geisio datrys y broblem hon? Mae diffyg argaeledd deintyddion GIG allan o reolaeth erbyn hyn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
The lack of accessibility to dentists is something that deeply worries me. I lost my NHS dentist a long time ago, as many of us here have, I know. What we're in the process of doing now is reviewing the contract. We need to make sure that we have a system that works for the patient and for the dentist, who we want to work within the NHS system in Wales.

There's more beside that. We need to be making sure that we have that pipeline of dentists coming through the system. That is why work led by the now Minister for local government, when she was in opposition, to bring a new dental school to Wales is something that is so key. The problems in dentistry are plain for all to see. I do believe we have a window in which we can try to act now, but be in no doubt about the scale of the challenge that we face around dentistry, because of the legacy of a lack of attention to this over many years, I fear.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Mae diffyg argaeledd deintyddion yn fater sy'n peri gofid mawr i mi. Fe gollais i fy neintydd GIG amser maith yn ôl, fel gwnaeth llawer ohonom ni yma, rwy'n gwybod. Yr hyn yr ydym ni yn y broses o'i wneud nawr yw adolygu'r contract. Mae angen i ni sicrhau bod system gennym ni sy'n gweithio er mwyn y claf a'r deintydd, yr ydym ni'n dymuno iddo weithio yng nghyfundrefn y GIG yng Nghymru.

Mae yna fwy ar ben hynny. Mae angen i ni sicrhau bod gennym ni'r ffrwd honno o ddeintyddion yn dod trwy'r system. Dyna pam mae gwaith a gafodd ei wneud dan arweiniad y Gweinidog llywodraeth leol erbyn hyn, pan oedd hi yn yr wrthblaid, i ddod ag ysgol ddeintyddol newydd i Gymru yn rhywbeth sydd mor allweddol. Mae'r problemau o ran deintyddiaeth yn amlwg i bawb eu gweld. Rwyf i o'r farn fod cyfle gennym ni i geisio gweithredu nawr, ond nid oes unrhyw amheuaeth am raddfa'r her yr ydym ni'n ei hwynebu ynghylch deintyddiaeth, o ganlyniad i brinder y sylw a roddwyd i hyn dros lawer o flynyddoedd, rwy'n ofni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Poverty

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 6. Beth yw cynlluniau Llywodraeth Cymru ar gyfer mynd i'r afael â thlodi yn nhymor y Senedd hon? OQ64674
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 6. What are the Welsh Government's plans for addressing poverty in this Senedd term? OQ64674

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Throughout our ambitious programme for government, we commit to take action to reduce financial pressures facing households, working to break the cycle of poverty that too many find themselves in. Our new child poverty strategy will set clear targets and milestones to drive ambitious, deliverable change. We'll also seek to introduce the Cynnal child payment pilot. This Government will help those in crisis, while taking longer term, strategic action to prevent people falling into poverty in the first place.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn ein rhaglen lywodraethu ni drwyddi draw, rydym ni'n ymrwymo i gymryd camau i ysgafnu'r pwysau ariannol sy'n wynebu aelwydydd, gan weithio i dorri'r cylch o dlodi y mae llawer gormod o bobl yn eu cael eu hunain ynddo. Fe fydd ein strategaeth tlodi plant newydd yn pennu nodau a cherrig milltir eglur i ysgogi newid uchelgeisiol, y gellir ei gyflawni. Fe fyddwn ni'n ceisio cyflwyno'r cynllun treialu taliad plant, Cynnal. Fe fydd y Llywodraeth hon yn cynorthwyo'r rhai sydd mewn argyfwng, wrth gymryd camau strategol yn y tymor hwy i rwystro pobl rhag syrthio i dlodi yn y lle cyntaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: It's fascinating that your answer did not explicitly state whether you're talking about absolute poverty or relative poverty, and they are very different metrics. Absolute poverty focuses on the welfare of the poorest people in our society, something I want to see all Governments focus on. The other, relative poverty, is in reality a type of inequality, focused on the gap in wealth between people, and that can be a very dangerous metric. As Margaret Thatcher said, those who focus on inequality above absolute poverty would rather the poor were poorer so long as the rich were even less rich, reducing the gap. First Minister, do you accept there is an important difference in the two measures of poverty? To avoid confusion in future, will you and your Government, when referencing poverty, state clearly whether you're talking about absolute poverty or the socialist obsession that is inequality?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae hi'n ddiddorol dros ben nad oedd eich ateb chi'n mynegi yn ddiamwys mai sôn am dlodi absoliwt yr oeddech chi neu am dlodi cymharol, ac mae'r rhain yn fetrigau gwahanol iawn. Mae tlodi absoliwt yn canolbwyntio ar les y bobl dlotaf yn ein cymdeithas, rhywbeth yr hoffwn i weld pob Llywodraeth yn canolbwyntio arno. Mae'r llall, tlodi cymharol, yn golygu anghydraddoldeb, mewn gwirionedd, wrth ganolbwyntio ar y bwlch cyfoeth rhwng pobl â'i gilydd, ac fe all hwnnw fod yn fetrig peryglus iawn. Fel dywedodd Margaret Thatcher, fe fyddai hi'n well gan y rhai sy'n canolbwyntio ar anghydraddoldeb yn fwy nag ar dlodi absoliwt i weld y tlawd yn dlotach cyn belled â bod y cyfoethog yn llai cyfoethog, sy'n lleihau'r bwlch. Brif Weinidog, a ydych chi'n derbyn bod gwahaniaeth pwysig rhwng y ddau fesur o dlodi? I osgoi amwyster yn y dyfodol, a wnewch chi a'ch Llywodraeth, wrth gyfeirio at dlodi, ddatgan yn eglur a ydych chi'n sôn am dlodi absoliwt neu am yr obsesiwn sosialaidd sef anghydraddoldeb?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I think the fact that the Member wants an academic discussion rather than a discussion about how we as a Government can really help those who are in dire need of that help from Government says a lot. The fact that he quotes Margaret Thatcher in an argument on tackling poverty speaks even further volumes. We have a series of measures that we have put in place. Our poverty strategy, setting the meaningful targets that the sector and others have called for, is going to be a really important part of that. We haven't had a trajectory for some years in Wales on where we need to go in terms of tackling poverty. What I know is that the problems are real. That's why the universal childcare offer cuts to some of the biggest challenges that families are facing, and why the Cynnal direct payment can be the beginnings of something that genuinely puts a safety net beneath some of our poorest families in Wales.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n credu bod y ffaith fod yr Aelod yn dymuno cynnal trafodaeth academaidd yn hytrach na thrafodaeth ynglŷn â'r ffyrdd y gallwn ni yn y Llywodraeth gynorthwyo'r rhai sydd ag angen gwirioneddol am y cymorth hwnnw gan y Llywodraeth yn dweud llawer iawn. Mae'r ffaith ei fod ef yn dyfynnu Margaret Thatcher mewn dadl ar fynd i'r afael â thlodi yn dweud y cyfan. Mae gennym ni gyfres o fesurau y gwnaethom ni eu rhoi ar waith. Fe fydd ein strategaeth tlodi, sy'n pennu'r nodau ystyrlon y mae'r sector ac eraill wedi galw amdanyn nhw, yn rhan bwysig iawn o hynny. Nid oes taflwybr wedi bod gennym ni yng Nghymru ers rhai blynyddoedd o ran mynd i'r afael â thlodi. Yr hyn yr wyf i'n ei wybod yw bod y problemau yn rhai gwirioneddol. Dyna pam mae'r cynnig gofal plant cyffredinol yn rhoi toriadau i rai o'r heriau mwyaf y mae teuluoedd yn eu hwynebu, a pham y gall taliad uniongyrchol Cynnal fod yn ddechrau ar rywbeth a fydd yn cynnig rhwyd achub wirioneddol i rai o'n teuluoedd tlotaf ni yng Nghymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Capasiti Presgripsiynu Cymdeithasol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Social Prescribing Capacity

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 7. Sut bydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn cefnogi capasiti presgripsiynu cymdeithasol yn Afan Ogwr Rhondda? OQ64651
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 7. How will the Welsh Government support social prescribing capacity in Afan Ogwr Rhondda? OQ64651

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mae'r Llywodraeth yma wedi ymrwymo i gefnogi presgripsiynu cymdeithasol ledled Cymru, yn gynnwys yn Afan Ogwr Rhondda. Mae hynny'n golygu helpu pobl i wella eu hiechyd a'u lles drwy gymorth yn y gymuned a thrwy ganolbwyntio ar atal. Mor ddiweddar â bore ddoe, mi wnaeth y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Iechyd Cyhoeddus ac Ataliol, Nerys Evans, ymweld â phrosiect rhagorol presgripsiynu cymdeithasol sy'n seiliedig ar natur, sef Grow Well, a hynny yn Dusty Forge yn Nhrelái yma yng Nghaerdydd. Rydyn ni'n buddsoddi mewn gwerthusiad annibynnol i asesu'r canlyniadau i unigolion, cymunedau a gwasanaethau rheng flaen, ac i drio deall yn well sut y gall presgripsiynu cymdeithasol wella lles a chefnogi gwasanaethau cynaliadwy.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: This Government is committed to supporting social prescribing across Wales, including in Afan Ogwr Rhondda, helping people to improve their health and well-being through community-based support and by focusing on prevention. As recently as yesterday morning, the Deputy Minister for Public and Preventative Health, Nerys Evans, visited an excellent project for social prescribing that is nature based, namely Grow Well at the Dusty Forge in Ely, here in Cardiff. We are investing in an independent evaluation to assess outcomes for individuals, communities and front-line services and to try and better understand how social prescribing can improve well-being and support sustainable services.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch am eich ymateb, Brif Weinidog. Er mwyn i bresgripsiynu cymdeithasol fod yn effeithiol, nid yn unig mae angen y gallu i wneud atgyfeiriadau arnom, ond mae hefyd angen rhwydwaith cryf a chynaliadwy o sefydliadau cymunedol sydd â'r adnoddau i allu eu derbyn. Yn ddiweddar, cwrddais â Kate o Gymdeithas Gymunedol Gilfach Goch, sy'n darparu ystod eang o gymorth i dros 1,500 o drigolion lleol, gyda'r galw yn parhau i gynyddu.

Sefydliadau fel hyn yw'r union leoedd y mae pobl yn cael eu hatgyfeirio iddynt, ond un o'r pryderon rwy'n eu clywed dro ar ôl tro yw y gall ffrydiau cyllidol ogwyddo'n sylweddol tuag at gyllid cyfalaf, gyda llawer llai o hyblygrwydd o ran y cyllid refeniw sydd ei angen i dalu staff, talu costau gweithredol a chadw gwasanaethau i fynd. Ychydig o ddefnydd sydd i adeilad os nad oes pobl ac adnoddau i gadw drysau ar agor a darparu'r gwasanaeth ynddo.

Felly, a all y Llywodraeth ystyried sut y gellid ymgorffori mwy o hyblygrwydd rhwng cyllid cyfalaf a refeniw mewn rhaglenni grant yn y dyfodol, fel bod gan sefydliadau fel Cymdeithas Gymunedol Gilfach Goch y gallu a'r sefydlogrwydd sydd eu hangen arnynt i ddiwallu'r galw cynyddol, ac fel bod presgripsiynu—lot o eiriau mawr heddiw—cymdeithasol yn arwain at barhad cymorth sy'n sail i agenda ataliol y Llywodraeth hon? Diolch.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you for your response, First Minister. For social prescribing to be effective, we not only need the ability to make referrals, but we also need a strong and sustainable network of community organisations that have the resources to be able to accept them. Recently, I met Kate from the Gilfach Goch Community Association, which provides a wide range of support to about 1,500 local residents, with the demand continuing to rise.

Institutions like this are exactly the sort of places people get referred to, but one of the concerns I hear again and again is that funding streams can lean heavily towards capital funding, with much less flexibility in terms of the revenue funding needed to pay staff, cover operational costs and keep services running. A building isn't much use if there aren't people and resources to keep the doors open and provide the services inside. 

So, could the Government consider how more flexibility could be built in between capital and revenue funding in grant programmes in the future, so that organisations like the Gilfach Goch Community Association have the capacity and stability they need to meet the growing demand, and so that—many large words here today—social prescribing leads to continuous support that underpins this Government's preventative agenda? Thank you.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch. Mae hi'n dda clywed am waith y ganolfan yn Gilfach Goch. Dwi’n cytuno bod presgripsiynu cymdeithasol effeithiol yn dibynnu ar sefydliadau cymunedol cryf a chynaliadwy sydd â chapasiti i ateb galw sydd yn cynyddu o hyd. Mae'r sector wirfoddol yn allweddol i'r model Cymreig yna. Dwi’n sicr yn cydnabod bod y pwysau yna o gwmpas cyllidebu tymor byr a diffyg hyblygrwydd weithiau o ran arian staffio ac arian rhedeg yn gallu creu problemau.

Mi fyddwn ni'n parhau fel Llywodraeth i weithio efo partneriaid ac i ystyried sut y gall newidiadau, o bosib, i drefniadau cyllido yn y dyfodol gefnogi yn well y capasiti a sefydlogrwydd sydd gan sefydliadau er mwyn iddyn nhw allu delifro ein hagenda ataliol ni. Achos nid y Llywodraeth yn gwneud hynny ydy'r stori gyfan; y stori ydy bod y Llywodraeth yn gosod y tôn, ac mae angen partneriaid arnom i wneud y gwaith ataliol ar lawr gwlad.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Thank you. It's good to hear about the work of the centre in Gilfach Goch. I agree that social prescribing, done effectively, does depend on strong community organisations that are sustainable and have the capacity to meet ever-increasing demand. The voluntary sector is key to that Welsh model. I certainly accept that the pressures around short-term budgeting and the lack of flexibility on occasion in terms of staffing and running costs can create problems.

We as a Government will continue to work with partners and to consider how possible changes to funding arrangements in future could better support that capacity and the stability available to these organisations, so that they can deliver our preventative agenda. Because the Government doing this is not the whole story; the story is that the Government sets the tone, and we need partners to do that work on the ground.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Mynediad at Addysg
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Access to Education

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 8. Pa asesiad y mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi'i wneud ynghylch a yw'r fframwaith teithio presennol i ddysgwyr yn darparu mynediad teg at addysg ledled Cymru? OQ64650
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 8. What assessment has the First Minister made of whether the current learner travel framework is delivering fair access to education across Wales? OQ64650

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Effective learner travel provision is vital to ensure that children and young people can access the education that they need. I understand there are also challenges for local authorities, given very real budget pressures. This is why we've committed to a joined-up approach to learner travel in our programme for government and why we've already delivered on our first 100 days commitment to review learner travel in Welsh-medium education in particular.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae darpariaeth effeithiol o deithio gan ddysgwyr yn hanfodol i sicrhau bod plant a phobl ifanc yn gallu cael mynediad at yr addysg y mae ei hangen arnyn nhw. Rwy'n deall bod heriau i'r awdurdodau lleol hefyd, o ystyried pwysau cyllidebol gwirioneddol iawn. Dyna pam rydym ni wedi ymrwymo i ddull cydgysylltiedig o deithio gan ddysgwyr yn ein rhaglen lywodraethu a pham rydym ni eisoes wedi cyflawni ar ein hymrwymiad 100 diwrnod cyntaf i adolygu teithio gan ddysgwyr o ran addysg cyfrwng Cymraeg yn arbennig.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The statutory threshold remains 2 miles for primary schools and 3 miles for secondary pupils. In communities such as Islwyn, the reality of their journey can be very different, depending on the terrain, the roads and whether there is a genuinely safe walking route. Will the First Minister look at whether the current framework is producing fair and consistent outcomes for children across Wales?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Dwy filltir ar gyfer ysgolion cynradd a thair milltir ar gyfer disgyblion uwchradd yw'r trothwy statudol o hyd. Mewn cymunedau fel Islwyn, fe all eu taith wirioneddol fod yn un wahanol iawn, gan ddibynnu ar y dirwedd, yr heolydd ac a oes yna lwybr gwirioneddol ddiogel i'w gerdded. A wnaiff y Prif Weinidog ystyried a yw'r fframwaith cyfredol yn arwain at ganlyniadau sy'n deg a chyson i blant ledled Cymru?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I certainly appreciate that journeys for pupils are different depending on their individual circumstances. We're looking at the existing framework in the context of the budgets available to us. The Deputy Minister for Transport has himself highlighted learner travel as one of his key priorities. We'll consider this as a Cabinet, because it does cut across portfolios.

I know that decisions are made on a local level by local authorities, some of whose decisions to deem walking routes safe do raise questions and anxiety. But these are decisions for those local authorities. It is for local authorities to assess whether a walking route is safe, taking account of the conditions learners would encounter on that journey to school at that time of day, and so on.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Yn sicr, rwy'n deall bod teithio gan ddisgyblion yn wahanol yn ddibynnol ar eu hamgylchiadau unigol. Rydym ni'n edrych ar y fframwaith presennol yng nghyd-destun y cyllidebau sydd ar gael i ni. Mae'r Dirprwy Weinidog Trafnidiaeth ei hun wedi tynnu sylw at deithio gan ddysgwyr fel un o'i brif flaenoriaethau ef. Fe fyddwn ni'n ystyried hyn yn y Cabinet, oherwydd mae'r pwnc yn croestorri portffolios.

Fe wn i fod penderfyniadau yn cael eu gwneud ar lefel leol gan yr awdurdodau lleol, a bod rhai o'u penderfyniadau nhw o ran ystyried a yw llwybrau yn ddiogel i'w cerdded yn ennyn ymholiadau a phryder. Ond penderfyniadau i'r awdurdodau lleol hynny yw'r rhain. Mae'n rhaid i'r awdurdodau lleol asesu a yw llwybr cerdded yn ddiogel, gan ystyried yr amgylchiadau y byddai dysgwyr yn eu hwynebu ar y daith honno i'r ysgol ac ar yr amser hwnnw o'r dydd, ac ati.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Camdriniaeth yn ystod Plentyndod
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Childhood Abuse

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 9. Pa gamau y mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn eu cymryd i gefnogi goroeswyr camdriniaeth yn ystod plentyndod sy'n profi trawma pellach wrth geisio cael mynediad at gofnodion gwaith cymdeithasol, iechyd neu'r heddlu hanesyddol? OQ64653
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 9. What action is the Welsh Government taking to support survivors of childhood abuse who experience further trauma when accessing historical social work, health or police records? OQ64653

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I lawer o oroeswyr, mae cael mynediad at gofnodion hanesyddol yn bwysig er mwyn deall eu plentyndod, ond mae'r broses yn gallu peri gofid mawr. Rydyn ni'n gwybod hynny. Rydyn ni'n cefnogi gwasanaethau cyhoeddus i fabwysiadu dulliau mwy ystyriol o drawma, fel bod pobl yn cael eu trin efo urddas, tosturi a sensitifrwydd. Mae'r gwaith yma yn cael ei ategu gan ein fframwaith Cymru sy'n ystyriol o drawma a'n strategaeth ar atal ac ymateb i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol. Mae'r ddau yn cydnabod effaith gydol oes cam-drin ac yn rhoi lle canolog i leisiau goroeswyr wrth wella gwasanaethau.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: For many survivors, accessing historical records is important in understanding their childhood, but the process can be deeply distressing. We know that. We are supporting public services to adopt trauma-informed approaches, so that people are treated with dignity, compassion and sensitivity. This work is reinforced through our trauma-informed Wales framework and our strategy for preventing and responding to child sexual abuse. Both recognise the lifelong impact of abuse and place survivors' voices at the centre of improvement.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, First Minister. Victims and survivors tell us that, when they raise concerns about victim-blaming language or missed opportunities to protect them within historical social work, health or police records, they are often told that these attitudes were simply a product of the time and would not be acceptable today. However, for survivors living with post-traumatic stress disorder, physical ill health and the lifelong consequences of abuse, the impact is very much felt today. Many access these records in an attempt to piece together their life story and to better understand their experiences, only to find that the files leave them with more questions than answers. For professionals, these may be historical records, but for survivors, the trauma is not historical at all. What more can the Welsh Government do to ensure survivors are met with recognition, trauma-informed support and meaningful acknowledgement of the harm these records can still cause?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Brif Weinidog. Mae dioddefwyr a goroeswyr yn dweud wrthym ni, pan fyddan nhw'n codi pryderon ynglŷn ag ieithwedd sy'n beio dioddefwyr neu ynglŷn â chyfleoedd a gollwyd i'w hamddiffyn nhw mewn cofnodion hanesyddol gan weithwyr cymdeithasol, iechyd neu'r heddlu, fe ddywedir yn aml mai dim ond o ganlyniad i'r syniadau ar y pryd y cafwyd yr agweddau hyn ac na fydden nhw'n dderbyniol heddiw. Er hynny, i oroeswyr sy'n byw gydag anhwylder straen ôl-drawmatig, salwch corfforol a chanlyniadau gydol oes oherwydd camdriniaeth, mae'r effaith yn ddirdynnol heddiw. Mae llawer yn cael gafael ar y cofnodion hyn ar gyfer ceisio rhoi darnau hanes eu bywydau at ei gilydd a deall eu profiadau yn well ac yn cael eu siomi wrth ddarganfod bod y ffeiliau yn cynnig mwy o gwestiynau nag atebion iddyn nhw. Ar gyfer gweithwyr proffesiynol, efallai mai cofnodion hanesyddol yw'r rhain, ond i oroeswyr, nid yw'r archoll yn hanesyddol o gwbl. Beth arall y gall Llywodraeth Cymru ei wneud i sicrhau bod goroeswyr yn cael y gydnabyddiaeth, y cymorth sy'n ystyriol o drawma a chydnabyddiaeth ystyrlon o'r niwed y gall y cofnodion hyn ei beri o hyd?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 1. Cwestiynau i'r Prif Weinidog
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 1. Questions to the First Minister
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: We recognise that the language, the assumptions or professional judgments contained in some historical records can be distressing and certainly can compound the impact of past trauma. Through the trauma-informed Wales framework and that strategy for preventing and responding to child sexual abuse, we are supporting services to respond with dignity, with compassion, with sensitivity, recognising, as I say, that the effects of abuse can be lifelong. We're also continuing to support life journey work for children in care, care leavers and adopted children, helping them to understand their personal history and experiences in a way that is sensitive, that is meaningful and that, crucially, is centred on their voice. These are matters that the Government is determined to take steps forward on, for very good reason, because we are talking about people who face vulnerabilities, and they deserve to sense that support from Government in all ways.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rydym ni'n cydnabod bod yr ieithwedd, y rhagdybiaethau neu'r dyfarniadau proffesiynol sy'n cael eu cynnwys mewn rhai cofnodion hanesyddol yn gallu peri gofid mawr ac yn sicr maen nhw'n gallu cymhlethu effaith archoll yn y gorffennol. Trwy Fframwaith Cymru sy'n ystyriol o drawma a'r strategaeth honno ar gyfer atal ac ymateb i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol, rydym ni'n cefnogi gwasanaethau i ymateb gydag urddas, gyda thosturi, gyda sensitifrwydd, gan gydnabod, fel rwy'n dweud, y gall effeithiau camdriniaeth barhau ar hyd oes rhywun. Hefyd, rydym ni'n parhau i gefnogi gwaith taith bywyd i blant mewn gofal, pobl sy'n gadael gofal a phlant mabwysiedig, gan eu helpu nhw i ddeall eu hanes a'u profiadau personol mewn ffordd sy'n sensitif, sy'n ystyrlon ac sy'n canolbwyntio ar eu lleisiau nhw. Mae'r rhain yn faterion y mae'r Llywodraeth yn benderfynol o fwrw ymlaen i weithredu arnyn nhw, a hynny am reswm da iawn, oherwydd siarad yr ydym ni am bobl sy'n wynebu bod yn agored i niwed, ac maen nhw'n haeddu cael yr ymdeimlad hwnnw o gefnogaeth gan y Llywodraeth ym mhob modd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_English: Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Member_job_title_Welsh: Y Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a’r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: The Welsh Government is committed to establishing a national commission for Wales and is taking forward the final arrangements necessary for its establishment. I will make a further statement to Senedd Members in due course, setting out the commission’s remit, membership and next steps.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi ymrwymo i sefydlu comisiwn cenedlaethol i Gymru ac mae hi'n bwrw ymlaen â'r trefniadau terfynol sy'n angenrheidiol ar gyfer sefydlu hwnnw. Fe fyddaf i'n gwneud datganiad pellach i Aelodau'r Senedd maes o law, yn nodi cylch gorchwyl y comisiwn, ei aelodaeth, a'r camau nesaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Cabinet Minister. Devolving the Crown Estate to Wales is very broadly and strongly supported all across the country. Every single one of our 22 unitary authorities in Wales have recently voted in favour of bringing powers over the Crown Estate to Wales. Since 2017, Scotland has had powers over its own estate, which lets the Scottish Government retain and reinvest the income generated. According to Crown Estate Scotland, in one 12-month period, it generated an economic impact of £2.1 billion and supported 17,000 jobs. We, on the other hand, are not so lucky. The profits generated from the Welsh part of the Crown Estate flow back to the UK Treasury, with a share allocated to the royal household. The income from retaining the full value of leasing our land and sea bed could be transformative for Wales, generating energy and reinvesting in our communities. Given that the demand is already so strong and supported all across Wales, what is the next step for making the case for devolution of the Crown Estate to Wales and making sure we get a fair settlement in line with Scotland's?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Weinidog Cabinet. Mae cefnogaeth eang a chryf iawn i ddatganoli Ystad y Goron i Gymru ledled y genedl. Yn ddiweddar, fe bleidleisiodd pob un o'r 22 awdurdod unedol yma yng Nghymru o blaid dod â phwerau dros Ystad y Goron i Gymru. Ers 2017, mae gan yr Alban bwerau dros ei hystad ei hun, sy'n caniatáu i Lywodraeth yr Alban gadw ac ailfuddsoddi'r incwm sy'n cael ei gynhyrchu. Yn ôl Crown Estate Scotland, mewn un cyfnod o 12 mis, fe gynhyrchodd effaith economaidd o £2.1 biliwn a chefnogodd 17,000 o swyddi. Nid ydym ni, ar y llaw arall, mor ffodus. Mae'r elw a gynhyrchir gan Ystad y Goron yng Nghymru yn llifo yn ôl i Drysorlys y DU, gyda chyfran yn cael ei dyrannu i weision y brenin. Fe allai'r incwm o gadw gwerth llawn prydlesu tir a gwely'r môr yma fod yn drawsnewidiol i Gymru, gan gynhyrchu ynni ac ailfuddsoddiad yn ein cymunedau ni. O ystyried bod y galw mor gryf eisoes ac yn cael ei gefnogi ledled Cymru, beth yw'r cam nesaf i ddadlau'r achos dros ddatganoli Ystad y Goron i Gymru a sicrhau ein bod ni'n cael setliad teg yn unol ag un yr Alban?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I thank the Member for the question. The case is very clearly made for the devolution of the Crown Estate. If you look over the past decade, there have been hundreds of millions of pounds of profits made by the Crown Estate in Wales. We believe that money should be invested in Wales and in Welsh energy and in supporting Welsh families and communities. The Welsh Government has established an expert group on the devolution of the Crown Estate and the future of the Crown Estate, which is building the evidence case. I expect a final report from the group to be published next summer. Then they will move forward to work on the broader issues of energy devolution.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n diolch i'r Aelod am y cwestiwn. Mae'r achos yn eglur iawn dros ddatganoli Ystad y Goron. Os edrychwch chi dros y degawd diwethaf, mae cannoedd o filiynau o bunnau o elw wedi cael eu gwneud gan Ystad y Goron yng Nghymru. Rydym ni o'r farn y dylid buddsoddi arian yng Nghymru ac yn ynni Cymru ac er mwyn cefnogi teuluoedd a chymunedau Cymru. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru wedi sefydlu grŵp arbenigol ar ddatganoli Ystad y Goron a dyfodol Ystad y Goron, sy'n adeiladu'r achos tystiolaeth. Rwy'n disgwyl i adroddiad terfynol gan y grŵp gael ei gyhoeddi'r haf nesaf. Fe fyddan nhw'n symud ymlaen wedyn i weithio ar faterion ehangach datganoli ynni.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: 2. Pa asesiad y mae'r Gweinidog Cabinet wedi'i wneud o effaith perthynas Llywodraeth Cymru ag undebau llafur ar effeithiolrwydd y Llywodraeth? OQ64620
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: 2. What assessment has the Cabinet Minister made of the impact on Government effectiveness of the Welsh Government's relationship with trade unions? OQ64620

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As a Government, we recognise the value that trade unions bring to Government effectiveness. They provide structures for meaningful dialogue, negotiation and problem solving, enabling early intervention that saves time and money. Social partnership ensures workforce voices are heard early in decision making and remains the most effective way to address Wales's challenges.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Yn y Llywodraeth, rydym ni'n cydnabod y gwerth y mae undebau llafur yn ei ddwyn i effeithiolrwydd y Llywodraeth. Maen nhw'n darparu strwythurau ar gyfer deialog ystyrlon, trafod a datrys problemau, gan alluogi ymyrraeth gynnar sy'n arbed amser ac arian. Mae partneriaeth gymdeithasol yn sicrhau bod lleisiau'r gweithlu yn cael eu clywed yn gynnar wrth wneud penderfyniadau a honno yw'r ffordd fwyaf effeithiol o hyd wrth fynd i'r afael â heriau Cymru.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Thank you, Minister, for your response. You might have noticed I've written a number of times to you—I've kept your office busy—and I've written to your office a number of times via written questions, and I thank your office for supplying information on that. From that information gathered, it has shown that, over the previous Labour Government, over the course of five years, around £13 million was provided to trade unions. In addition to that information, it has also shown that they have also funded up to 10 equivalent full-time posts. What I do find a little bit concerning is that there's no definite time spent on trade union work and that of their civil service work. My question to you is, Minister, will your Government be spending any more taxpayers' money on political trade unions?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Diolch i chi, Weinidog, am eich ymateb. Efallai eich bod chi wedi dal sylw fy mod i wedi ysgrifennu atoch chi sawl gwaith—rwyf i wedi cadw eich swyddfa chi'n brysur—ac rwyf i wedi ysgrifennu at eich swyddfa chi sawl gwaith trwy gyfrwng cwestiynau ysgrifenedig, ac rwy'n diolch i'ch swyddfa am ddarparu gwybodaeth ynglŷn â hynny. O'r wybodaeth honno a gasglwyd, roedd yn dangos, dros y Llywodraeth Lafur flaenorol, dros gyfnod o bum mlynedd, bod tua £13 miliwn wedi cael ei roi i undebau llafur. Yn ogystal â'r wybodaeth honno, roedd yn dangos hefyd eu bod nhw wedi ariannu'r hyn sy'n cyfateb i 10 swydd amser llawn. Yr hyn yr wyf i'n ei ystyried ychydig yn bryderus yw nad oes amser penodol yn cael ei dreulio ar waith undebau llafur na'u gwaith gwasanaeth sifil. Fy nghwestiwn i chi yw, Weinidog, a fydd eich Llywodraeth chi'n gwario mwy o arian trethdalwyr ar undebau llafur gwleidyddol?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: As I said in my first response, this Government remains committed to social partnership. It is something that we believe in, in principle and on principle. There will be Members across this Chamber who have led organisations and who have managed organisations with trade unions and built effective relationships with those trade unions. We will make no apology for supporting trade unions, for working with them. There will be times, as everyone knows, when we will not see eye to eye on everything with those trade unions, but a strong and happy workforce is an effective workforce, and I'm proud to say that this Government will work with our trade union partners.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fel dywedais i yn fy ymateb cyntaf, mae'r Llywodraeth hon yn dal i fod yn ymrwymedig i bartneriaeth gymdeithasol. Mae hwnnw'n rhywbeth yr ydym ni'n credu ynddo, mewn egwyddor ac ar egwyddor. Fe fydd yna Aelodau ar draws y Siambr hon sydd wedi arwain sefydliadau ac sydd wedi rheoli sefydliadau gyda'r undebau llafur ac wedi meithrin perthynas effeithiol â'r undebau llafur hynny. Ni fyddwn ni'n gwneud unrhyw ymddiheuriad am gefnogi undebau llafur, nac am weithio gyda nhw. Fe fydd yna adegau, fel gŵyr pawb, pryd na fyddwn ni'n cytuno yn llwyr ar bopeth gyda'r undebau llafur hynny, ond mae gweithlu cryf a hapus yn weithlu effeithiol, ac rwy'n falch o ddweud y bydd y Llywodraeth hon yn gweithio gyda'n partneriaid yn yr undebau llafur.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 2. Cwestiynau i’r Gweinidog Cabinet dros Effeithiolrwydd Llywodraeth a'r Cyfansoddiad
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 2. Questions to the Cabinet Minister for Government Effectiveness and the Constitution
