XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Minister, for your statement. I definitely concur with you that safeguarding is one of the most important responsibilities of any Government, and I wanted to focus my remarks on children today. You've just said then that you get lessons from the various reviews that are brought forward, and, unfortunately, recent child practice reviews have identified a number of recurring themes, including problems with information sharing, inconsistent application of safeguarding thresholds, and insufficient focus on the child's voice. And therein lies our challenge, doesn't it, really? It's taking policy into practice and making sure that that is implemented in a way that keeps children safe.

It was very good to see you accepting all the recommendations of the Jan Pickles safeguarding review, including on a ministerial safeguarding board. And of course, in 2024, under the previous Government, Wales was the first in the UK to introduce a single unified safeguarding review process, and that included the Wales safeguarding repository. So, I wanted to ask about the commitment in your statement to a national social care intelligence hub and how that would build on the work of the safeguarding repository.

I note as well the commitment to an adult and child protection authority for Wales, and that wasn't recommended in Jan Pickles's review, but it was a recommendation of the independent inquiry into child sexual abuse, and I would certainly support anything that strengthens protections for children and young people. But it would be good to hear you say a little bit about why you've taken that decision to go down that particular road. We're all acutely aware that social care services are stretched financially, and so are those vital services that deal with early intervention with families. So, I'd be keen to hear more about whether you're planning to announce dedicated funding for stronger safeguarding for a safer Wales.

Now, it's been nearly a year since I stood up in the Senedd to make a statement on 'Our Bravery Brought Justice'. That report was the most sobering thing I had ever read since becoming an MS, and parts of it, literally, took my breath away. Now, the overriding failure, really, that ran right the way through that report was the failure to listen to the voice of the child on, literally, countless occasions. Now, you've referred to the importance of children's voice today and embedding that in the work that you're doing, but what I would like to hear is some more detail as to how you are going to do that, because children's voice can't just be an issue for agencies out there—it has to be embedded in the Government's efforts to safeguard children.

Criminal and sexual exploitation of children remains a very serious issue, and one of the problems in this area is the fact that so many vulnerable children, looked-after children, children on the edge of care, are going missing too often. Now, there have been calls for statutory return-home interviews, because, at the moment, there are different practices amongst local authorities and police forces. Can I ask if that is something that you will consider as part of the work that you're doing on children?

And I can see that the Cabinet Minister for education is in the Chamber today, which is good to see. Obviously, it's crucial that there is joint working across Government to protect children. I know that you're still committed to the follow-on work on safeguarding in education, but can I ask how you intend to work with the Cabinet Minister on those issues in education, and particularly on things that we know expose children to more risks, such as exclusion, which can lead to them being more vulnerable to exploitation? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog, am eich datganiad. Rwy'n bendant yn cytuno â chi mai diogelu yw un o gyfrifoldebau pwysicaf unrhyw Lywodraeth, ac roeddwn i eisiau canolbwyntio fy sylwadau ar blant heddiw. Rydych chi newydd ddweud yn y fan yna eich bod chi'n cael gwersi o'r gwahanol adolygiadau sy'n cael eu cyflwyno, ac, yn anffodus, mae adolygiadau diweddar ar ymarfer plant wedi nodi nifer o themâu cyson, gan gynnwys problemau gyda rhannu gwybodaeth, cymhwyso trothwyon diogelu yn anghyson, a ffocws annigonol ar lais y plentyn. A dyna lle mae'r her, ynte, mewn gwirionedd? Rhoi polisi ar waith a gwneud yn siŵr ei fod yn cael ei weithredu mewn ffordd sy'n cadw plant yn ddiogel.

Roedd yn dda iawn eich gweld yn derbyn holl argymhellion adolygiad diogelu Jan Pickles, gan gynnwys ar fwrdd diogelu gweinidogol. Ac wrth gwrs, yn 2024, o dan y Llywodraeth flaenorol, Cymru oedd y gyntaf yn y DU i gyflwyno un broses adolygu diogelu unedig, ac roedd hynny'n cynnwys storfa ddiogelu Cymru. Felly, roeddwn i eisiau gofyn am yr ymrwymiad yn eich datganiad i hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol cenedlaethol a sut y byddai hynny'n adeiladu ar waith y storfa ddiogelu.

Nodaf hefyd yr ymrwymiad i awdurdod amddiffyn oedolion a phlant i Gymru, ac ni chafodd hynny ei argymell yn adolygiad Jan Pickles, ond roedd yn un o argymhellion yr ymchwiliad annibynnol i gam-drin plant yn rhywiol, a byddwn i'n sicr yn cefnogi unrhyw beth sy'n cryfhau amddiffyniadau i blant a phobl ifanc. Ond byddai'n dda eich clywed chi'n dweud ychydig am pam rydych chi wedi gwneud y penderfyniad hwnnw i fynd i lawr y ffordd benodol honno. Rydyn ni i gyd yn ymwybodol iawn bod gwasanaethau gofal cymdeithasol yn cael eu hymestyn yn ariannol, ac felly hefyd y gwasanaethau hanfodol hynny sy'n delio ag ymyrraeth gynnar gyda theuluoedd. Felly, byddwn i'n awyddus i glywed mwy ynghylch a ydych chi'n bwriadu cyhoeddi cyllid penodol ar gyfer diogelu cryfach ar gyfer Cymru fwy diogel.

Nawr, mae bron i flwyddyn wedi mynd heibio ers i mi sefyll i fyny yn y Senedd i wneud datganiad ar 'Cyfiawnder trwy ein Dewrder'. Yr adroddiad hwnnw oedd y peth mwyaf sobreiddiol i mi erioed ei ddarllen ers dod yn AS, ac fe wnaeth rannau ohono, yn llythrennol, fynd â fy anadl. Nawr, y methiant pennaf, mewn gwirionedd, a redodd drwy'r adroddiad hwnnw oedd y methiant i wrando ar lais y plentyn, yn llythrennol, ar achlysuron dirifedi. Nawr, rydych chi wedi cyfeirio at bwysigrwydd llais plant heddiw ac ymwreiddio hynny yn y gwaith rydych chi'n ei wneud, ond yr hyn yr hoffwn ei glywed yw ychydig mwy o fanylion ynghylch sut rydych chi'n mynd i wneud hynny, oherwydd ni all llais plant fod yn fater i asiantaethau allan yna yn unig—mae'n rhaid ei ymwreiddio yn ymdrechion y Llywodraeth i ddiogelu plant.

Mae camfanteisio'n droseddol ac yn rhywiol ar blant yn parhau i fod yn fater difrifol iawn, ac un o'r problemau yn y maes hwn yw'r ffaith bod cynifer o blant sy'n agored i niwed, plant sy'n derbyn gofal, plant ar gyrion gofal, yn mynd ar goll yn rhy aml. Nawr, mae galwadau wedi bod am gyfweliadau dychwelyd adref statudol, oherwydd, ar hyn o bryd, mae yna arferion gwahanol ymhlith awdurdodau lleol a'r heddluoedd. A allaf ofyn a yw hynny'n rhywbeth y byddwch chi'n ei ystyried fel rhan o'r gwaith rydych chi'n ei wneud ar blant?

Ac rwy'n gallu gweld bod y Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg yn y Siambr heddiw, sy'n dda i'w weld. Yn amlwg, mae'n hanfodol bod cydweithio ar draws y Llywodraeth i amddiffyn plant. Rwy'n gwybod eich bod chi'n dal i ymrwymo i'r gwaith dilynol ar ddiogelu mewn addysg, ond a gaf fi ofyn sut rydych chi'n bwriadu gweithio gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet ar y materion hynny ym maes addysg, ac yn enwedig ar bethau rydym yn gwybod eu bod yn gwneud plant yn agored i fwy o risgiau, fel allgáu, a all arwain at sefyllfa lle maen nhw'n fwy agored i gamfanteisio? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lynne, and I know that this is something that—. You have tremendous expertise in this area and dedication over many years, and I thank you for that. Of course, what we are doing here is building on a lot of work that was done by the previous Government and, again, I'm grateful to you for leading a lot of that work.

And in terms of how the—. I'm grateful that you've welcomed a number of the separate components of what I've been announcing today. You asked specifically a little more about how the central intelligence hub will work in practice. As I've set out, in terms of spotting patterns and gaps and helping to set priorities, a lot of this data or the intelligence already exists, but if we were to ensure that—. That would include things like insights arising from single unified safeguarding reviews. If we can bring those insights together to develop a greater national understanding of where different patterns are and where these risks are emerging, so that—. Because it's, deeply worryingly, something where so many risks evolve and emerge, we need to keep looking to make sure that something doesn't get lost or thought of as, 'Oh, well, that's something that is isolated. That couldn't possibly happen here.' We can never think in that way.

And I suppose this intelligence hub, which would be under the National Office of Care and Support, would be—. We'd want a dedicated safeguarding arm of that to bring all of that intelligence together. It would do things like spotting risks that cross organisational boundaries, that cross geographical boundaries, and make sure that that evidence helps to set priorities nationally, and make sure as well that—. I said earlier that a lot of this information is already available publicly. We are going to be establishing—well, I think we're, certainly, looking at establishing—a number of task-and-finish groups to look at how exactly this data can be used, how we can be guided, and I would welcome any Members with expertise in this area, including you, Lynne, if you have thoughts on how that should evolve, I'd really like to draw on your expertise with that.

You asked particularly about 'Our Bravery Brought Justice' and the voice of the child, which, if there is one thing that is a common theme running throughout this work and this, whether we look at it as a structure, whether we look at it as architecture, the fundamental cornerstone of all of it is making sure that children, when something goes wrong, either their voice is heard if they've raised that concern themselves, or someone is looking out for them and that gets heard and that gets spotted. It is something that—. I'm really determined that we have to make sure that this system is informed by those voices.

If we look at 'Our Bravery Brought Justice', the name of that report says it all. Children should never have had to have been that brave in the first place. We have to make sure that something like that doesn't happen again. We have to take every action possible to try to make sure that that doesn't happen again. And again, very often, we need to make sure that the services we have—. Even if they're well-meaning, they're not always trauma-informed, they're not always person-centred. We need to make sure that this is something that, again, as you have alluded to, is cross-Government. It's something that I'll be working really closely with the Cabinet Minister for education on, certainly, but across health, across social care, across so many different aspects, this is something that will come into so many elements of children's and young people's and adults' lives. Phase 2 of the review is looking at sport, at faith, at religious groups. We need to be looking across different sectors.

You asked about statutory return-home interviews, and, yes, that is something that is definitely under consideration. I think it is £700,000 that has been set aside for the work on safeguarding, but there is other work from other budget expenditure lines that is coming together, because, of course, this is, again, a cross-Government initiative.

But I would say, again, that there are Members across this Chamber who have had disclosures made to them, who have had horrendous experiences themselves or have known people who have gone through terrible things, and you will know more than anyone that we owe it to people who have gone through something terrible to get it right for people in the future. Their voices have to shape those improvements. So, diolch, Lynne, for those questions.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lynne, ac rwy'n gwybod bod hyn yn rhywbeth sydd—. Mae gennych chi arbenigedd aruthrol yn y maes hwn ac ymroddiad dros nifer o flynyddoedd, ac rwy'n diolch i chi am hynny. Wrth gwrs, yr hyn rydyn ni'n ei wneud yma yw adeiladu ar lawer o waith a gafodd ei wneud gan y Llywodraeth flaenorol ac, unwaith eto, rwy'n ddiolchgar i chi am arwain llawer o'r gwaith hwnnw.

Ac o ran sut mae'r—. Rwy'n ddiolchgar eich bod chi wedi croesawu nifer o'r elfennau ar wahân o'r hyn rwyf wedi bod yn ei gyhoeddi heddiw. Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn yn benodol am ychydig mwy am y ffordd y bydd yr hwb gwybodaeth canolog yn gweithio yn ymarferol. Fel rwyf wedi nodi, o ran adnabod patrymau a bylchau a helpu i osod blaenoriaethau, mae llawer o'r data hwn neu'r wybodaeth eisoes yn bodoli, ond pe baem ni'n sicrhau bod—. Byddai hynny'n cynnwys pethau fel mewnwelediadau sy'n deillio o adolygiadau diogelu unedig sengl. Os gallwn ni ddod â'r mewnwelediadau hynny at ei gilydd i ddatblygu mwy o ddealltwriaeth genedlaethol o ble mae gwahanol batrymau a ble mae'r risgiau hyn yn dod i'r amlwg, fel bod—. Oherwydd, mae'n peri gofid mawr, rhywbeth lle mae cynifer o risgiau'n esblygu ac yn dod i'r amlwg, mae angen i ni barhau i edrych i wneud yn siŵr nad yw rhywbeth yn cael ei golli neu'n cael ei ystyried fel, 'O, wel, mae hynny'n rhywbeth neilltuol. Allai hynny byth ddigwydd yma.' Allwn ni byth feddwl yn y ffordd honno.

Ac rwy'n tybio y byddai'r hwb gwybodaeth hwn, a fyddai o dan y Swyddfa Gofal a Chymorth Genedlaethol, yn—. Byddem ni eisiau cangen ddiogelu bwrpasol o hynny i ddod â'r holl wybodaeth honno at ei gilydd. Byddai'n gwneud pethau fel nodi risgiau sy'n croesi ffiniau sefydliadol, sy'n croesi ffiniau daearyddol, ac yn gwneud yn siŵr bod y dystiolaeth honno'n helpu i osod blaenoriaethau yn genedlaethol, ac yn gwneud yn siŵr hefyd fod—. Fe ddywedais i'n gynharach bod llawer o'r wybodaeth hon eisoes ar gael yn gyhoeddus. Rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn sefydlu—wel, rwy'n credu ein bod ni, yn sicr, yn edrych ar sefydlu—nifer o grwpiau gorchwyl a gorffen i edrych ar sut yn union y gellir defnyddio'r data hwn, sut y gallwn ni gael ein tywys, a byddwn i'n croesawu unrhyw Aelodau sydd ag arbenigedd yn y maes hwn, gan gynnwys chi, Lynne, os oes gennych chi feddyliau ar sut y dylai hynny esblygu, byddwn i wir yn hoffi tynnu ar eich arbenigedd gyda hynny.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn yn benodol am 'Cyfiawnder trwy ein Dewrder' a llais y plentyn, ac os oes un peth sy'n thema gyffredin sy'n rhedeg trwy gydol y gwaith hwn, a hyn, p'un a ydyn ni'n edrych arno fel strwythur, p'un a ydyn ni'n edrych arno fel pensaernïaeth, conglfaen sylfaenol y cyfan, yw gwneud yn siŵr bod plant, pan fydd rhywbeth yn mynd o'i le, naill ai bod eu llais yn cael ei glywed os ydyn nhw wedi codi'r pryder hwnnw eu hunain, neu fod rhywun yn edrych allan amdanyn nhw ac mae hynny'n cael ei glywed ac mae hynny'n cael ei nodi. Mae'n rhywbeth sydd—. Rwy'n benderfynol iawn bod yn rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y system hon yn cael ei llywio gan y lleisiau hynny.

Os edrychwn ni ar 'Cyfiawnder trwy ein Dewrder', mae enw'r adroddiad hwnnw'n dweud y cyfan. Ni ddylai plant byth fod wedi gorfod bod mor ddewr yn y lle cyntaf. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud yn siŵr nad yw rhywbeth fel yna yn digwydd eto. Mae'n rhaid i ni gymryd pob cam posibl i geisio sicrhau nad yw hynny'n digwydd eto. Ac eto, yn aml iawn, mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y gwasanaethau sydd gennym—. Hyd yn oed os oes ganddyn nhw fwriadau da, dydyn nhw ddim bob amser yn ystyriol o drawma, dydyn nhw ddim bob amser yn canolbwyntio ar yr unigolyn. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod hyn yn rhywbeth sydd, unwaith eto, fel yr ydych wedi cyfeirio ato, yn draws-lywodraethol. Mae'n rhywbeth y byddaf yn gweithio'n agos iawn gyda'r Gweinidog Cabinet dros addysg arno, yn sicr, ond ar draws iechyd, ar draws gofal cymdeithasol, ar draws cymaint o wahanol agweddau, mae hyn yn rhywbeth a fydd yn dod i mewn i gymaint o elfennau o fywydau plant a phobl ifanc ac oedolion. Mae Cam 2 yr adolygiad yn edrych ar chwaraeon, ar ffydd, ar grwpiau crefyddol. Mae angen i ni fod yn edrych ar draws gwahanol sectorau.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am gyfweliadau dychwelyd adref statudol, ac, ydy, mae hynny'n rhywbeth sy'n bendant yn cael ei ystyried. Rwy'n credu mai £700,000 sydd wedi'i neilltuo ar gyfer y gwaith ar ddiogelu, ond mae yna waith arall o linellau gwariant cyllidebol eraill sy'n dod at ei gilydd, oherwydd, wrth gwrs, mae hon, unwaith eto, yn fenter draws-lywodraethol.

Ond byddwn i'n dweud, eto, bod yna Aelodau ar draws y Siambr hon y mae datgeliadau wedi'u gwneud iddyn nhw, sydd wedi cael profiadau erchyll eu hunain neu sydd wedi adnabod pobl sydd wedi mynd trwy bethau ofnadwy, ac fe fyddwch chi'n gwybod yn fwy nag unrhyw un bod arnom ddyled i bobl sydd wedi mynd trwy rywbeth ofnadwy i gael pethau'n iawn i bobl yn y dyfodol. Mae'n rhaid i'w lleisiau nhw lunio'r gwelliannau hynny. Felly, diolch, Lynne, am y cwestiynau hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you, Deputy Minister, for this afternoon's statement. Putting stronger safeguards in place is something to be welcomed, but it must be more than just about structures, strategies and warm words from the Welsh Government. It is about whether a child or vulnerable adult at risk is identified early, whether concerns are acted upon and whether there is a joined-up approach from agencies working at pace to help keep people safe.

We must also learn from the past. I don't intend to go over the specific details today, as I am sure we are all aware of the situation, but we must learn from incidents such as the Neil Foden case. Following Foden's imprisonment for 17 years after being convicted of 19 sexual abuse offences, a child practice review was indeed held. That review found that there were more than 50 missed opportunities to intervene and stop the predator headteacher from sexually abusing children. The failings we saw in this were utterly sickening, and we must agree that it never—and I mean never—is allowed to be repeated ever again. So, how will the Welsh Government ensure that cases like these are taken into account as part of this piece of work?

In April 2025, the Supreme Court ruled that sex is defined as biological sex only—a welcome decision for women and girls across Wales. However, since then, we have seen dither and delay from the Welsh Government and other public bodies in ensuring that this ruling is adhered to, especially when it comes to single-sex spaces. So, Deputy Minister, do you agree with me that ensuring that the judgment is adhered to and implemented consistently across Wales is an important part of improving safeguarding?

Deputy Minister, whilst I welcome the Government's aim of delivering stronger safeguarding for a safer Wales, there are some important questions about how this is actually going to work. You say that the Government will strengthen national leadership, oversight and accountability, but who will ultimately be accountable if safeguarding arrangements fail, and what consequences will there be when agencies do not perform effectively? Deputy Minister, I am curious to know what, if anything, these proposed reforms will mean for staff on the front line, like social workers and teachers. What specific improvements will they see as a result of this piece of work?

Sticking with those on the front line, another obvious question is about whether the system has sufficient capacity. We know that there are severe staff shortages across the board, so is the workforce there to successfully bring these changes forward? If not, where will the extra capacity needed be coming from?

Also, Deputy Minister, what are the financial implications of these reforms? In your statement, you outlined plans to create a national social care intelligence hub, a national safeguarding plan and a national safeguarding risk register. When do you expect all of these to be operational? I'd really like to have some dates in place.

A joined-up approach between the various agencies is going to be instrumental in improving safeguards. That means better data sharing, which is something we all know previous Welsh Governments have seriously lacked on over the years. So, how will these reforms provide this joined-up approach when it comes to data sharing between sectors like health, education, social care and policing? I welcome the Government's commitment to ensuring consistency and protection across all parts of Wales. Nobody—and I mean nobody—should be at a disadvantage just because of their postcode. So, how is the Government going to measure whether these safeguards are applied consistently across the country?

Deputy Minister, talking about lived experience, it will be vital in relation to this going forward, and the voices of children and adults should be heard and should be at the heart of these reforms. So, can I please get a commitment from you that it will be the case and, if so, can you elaborate on how exactly they're going to be feeding into this? Deputy Minister, the proof will ultimately be in the pudding. The $1 million question is whether these reforms will make people feel safe in the long term, and I sincerely hope that they do, but what specific outcomes does the Government expect to improve and by when? Thank you.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Weinidog, am y datganiad y prynhawn yma. Mae rhoi mesurau diogelu cryfach ar waith yn rhywbeth i'w groesawu, ond mae'n rhaid iddo fod yn ymwneud â mwy na dim ond strwythurau, strategaethau a geiriau cynnes gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Mae'n ymwneud â ph'un a yw plentyn neu oedolyn agored i niwed sy'n wynebu risg yn cael ei nodi'n gynnar, p'un a oes gweithredu pan fydd pryderon a ph'un a yw asiantaethau sy'n gweithio ar gyflymder i helpu i gadw pobl yn ddiogel yn gweithredu mewn ffordd gydgysylltiedig.

Rhaid i ni hefyd ddysgu o'r gorffennol. Dydw i ddim yn bwriadu mynd dros y manylion penodol heddiw, gan fy mod i'n siŵr ein bod ni i gyd yn ymwybodol o'r sefyllfa, ond mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu o ddigwyddiadau fel achos Neil Foden. Ar ôl i Foden gael ei garcharu am 17 mlynedd ar ôl ei gael yn euog o 19 o droseddau o gam-drin rhywiol, cynhaliwyd adolygiad ymarfer plant. Canfu'r adolygiad hwnnw fod mwy na 50 o gyfleoedd wedi cael eu colli i ymyrryd ac atal y pennaeth a'r rheibiwr rhag cam-drin plant yn rhywiol. Roedd y methiannau a welsom yn hyn yn hollol afiach, ac mae'n rhaid i ni gytuno na fydd byth—ac rwy'n golygu byth—yn cael ei adael i ddigwydd byth eto. Felly, sut fydd Llywodraeth Cymru yn sicrhau bod achosion fel hyn yn cael eu hystyried fel rhan o'r darn hwn o waith?

Ym mis Ebrill 2025, dyfarnodd y Goruchaf Lys fod rhyw yn cael ei ddiffinio fel rhyw biolegol yn unig—penderfyniad i'w groesawu i fenywod a merched ledled Cymru. Fodd bynnag, ers hynny, rydyn ni wedi gweld petruso ac oedi gan Lywodraeth Cymru a chyrff cyhoeddus eraill wrth sicrhau bod cydymffurfiaeth â'r dyfarniad hwn, yn enwedig pan ddaw i fannau un rhyw. Felly, Ddirprwy Weinidog, ydych chi'n cytuno â mi fod sicrhau bod cydymffurfiaeth â'r dyfarniad a'i fod yn cael ei weithredu'n gyson ledled Cymru yn rhan bwysig o wella diogelu?

Ddirprwy Weinidog, er fy mod i'n croesawu nod y Llywodraeth o ddarparu diogelu cryfach ar gyfer Cymru fwy diogel, mae yna rai cwestiynau pwysig ynglŷn â sut mae hyn yn mynd i weithio mewn gwirionedd. Rydych chi'n dweud y bydd y Llywodraeth yn cryfhau arweinyddiaeth genedlaethol, goruchwyliaeth ac atebolrwydd, ond pwy fydd yn atebol yn y pen draw os bydd trefniadau diogelu yn methu, a beth fydd y canlyniadau pan na fydd asiantaethau yn perfformio'n effeithiol? Ddirprwy Weinidog, rwy'n chwilfrydig i wybod beth, os unrhyw beth, y bydd y diwygiadau arfaethedig hyn yn ei olygu i staff ar y rheng flaen, fel gweithwyr cymdeithasol ac athrawon. Pa welliannau penodol y byddan nhw'n eu gweld o ganlyniad i'r darn hwn o waith?

Gan aros gyda'r rhai ar y rheng flaen, cwestiwn amlwg arall yw a oes gan y system ddigon o gapasiti. Rydyn ni'n gwybod bod prinder staff difrifol yn gyffredinol, felly a yw'r gweithlu yno i gyflwyno'r newidiadau hyn yn llwyddiannus? Os na, o ble fydd y capasiti ychwanegol sydd ei angen yn dod?

Hefyd, Ddirprwy Weinidog, beth yw goblygiadau ariannol y diwygiadau hyn? Yn eich datganiad, fe wnaethoch chi amlinellu cynlluniau i greu hwb gwybodaeth gofal cymdeithasol cenedlaethol, cynllun diogelu cenedlaethol a chofrestr risg diogelu genedlaethol. Pryd ydych chi'n disgwyl i'r rhain i gyd fod yn weithredol? Hoffwn i gael rhai dyddiadau.

Mae dull gweithredu cydgysylltiedig rhwng y gwahanol asiantaethau yn mynd i fod yn allweddol wrth wella mesurau diogelu. Mae hynny'n golygu rhannu data yn well, sy'n rhywbeth rydyn ni i gyd yn gwybod nad yw llywodraethau blaenorol Cymru wedi gwneud yn dda arno dros y blynyddoedd. Felly, sut fydd y diwygiadau hyn yn darparu'r dull cydgysylltiedig hwn pan ddaw i rannu data rhwng sectorau fel iechyd, addysg, gofal cymdeithasol a phlismona? Rwy'n croesawu ymrwymiad y Llywodraeth i sicrhau cysondeb a diogelwch ar draws pob rhan o Gymru. Ni ddylai neb—ac rwy'n golygu neb—fod dan anfantais oherwydd eu cod post. Felly, sut mae'r Llywodraeth yn mynd i fesur a yw'r mesurau diogelu hyn yn cael eu cymhwyso'n gyson ledled y wlad?

Ddirprwy Weinidog, wrth siarad am brofiad bywyd, bydd yn hanfodol mewn perthynas â hyn yn y dyfodol, a dylai lleisiau plant ac oedolion gael eu clywed a dylen nhw fod wrth wraidd y diwygiadau hyn. Felly, a allaf gael ymrwymiad gennych chi y bydd hyn yn digwydd ac, os felly, allwch chi ymhelaethu ar sut yn union maen nhw'n mynd i fod yn bwydo i mewn i hyn? Ddirprwy Weinidog, yn y pen draw, wrth ei flas mae profi pwdin. Y cwestiwn mawr yw a fydd y diwygiadau hyn yn gwneud i bobl deimlo'n ddiogel yn y tymor hir, ac rwyf wir yn gobeithio y byddan nhw, ond pa ganlyniadau penodol y mae'r Llywodraeth yn disgwyl eu gwella ac erbyn pryd? Diolch.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Natasha, for those questions. As you've said, this has to be about making improvements to people's lives. This can't just be about what's down on a piece of paper, it can't just be what is collected in graphs. It's about whether what is collected is analysed effectively, whether it leads to action and whether that action translates into saving and improving people's lives, because that's the stuff that we're really talking about here. So, none of us will lose sight of that, of course. You've alluded to cases in the past where too many missed opportunities have been missed opportunities to act. We have to learn from those. We have to do everything in our power to save children and adults at risk in the future.

And, yes, this Government has committed to adhering to the law—always, of course. And we have also committed always to protecting those groups and those people who are at greatest risk and who are vulnerable in our society, and there are many facets to this. That is something that the Deputy First Minister has always been consistent on.

In terms of what you asked about what this will mean for front-line staff, well, this, of course, will mean empowering front-line staff. Because there will be so many missed opportunities that staff themselves will have flagged, when different staff might have spotted something, whether that was in one area or the same patterns emerging in different places. This will mean that we are ensuring that those staff voices will be amplified and that they won't be standing in isolation any more.

And, of course, as I mentioned to Claire, we're going to have to look at training and making sure that staff, in order to be empowered, are able to use the—. To make sure that they are aware of how this is going to change their work, but it is about empowering them and not putting further burdens on them. Because, of course, a lot of this, in terms of—. You asked about capacity. This is workable because an awful lot of this is not creating new obligations; this is about when staff are spotting things, when staff are doing their jobs, that we are gaining that national picture and that we have greater cohesiveness across the piece. So, it isn't about creating new forms or anything like that that staff will need to fill in; it's about making sure that every contact counts and that every voice is listened to.

You asked some specific questions about when, and I mentioned earlier that this is going to be a phased programme of work, so that where there are things we can do immediately, we can act very quickly on those at the same time as progressing some of the work that, as I've mentioned, is going to take further time and further consultation in some of these areas as well. In terms of the ministerial oversight board, the plan is to establish that certainly by the beginning of next year.

In terms of the national safeguarding plan and the national risk register, the time frame—. So, I think that we are determining at the moment whether it will cover three years or five years, but there will be annual deliverables and it's something that we are going to be working on over the next two years to establish, in terms of making sure that we know what a good system looks like. Again, that is with the hope of consulting on an adult and child protection authority in the future. So, again, this is phased because we don't want to do something that is then going to—. We don't want to have to throw the baby out with the bath water. So, that is why—. And I hope I haven't asked—.

And in terms of how children's voices will actually be listened to, whether they are actually going to matter in this process, as I mentioned to Lynne, we are going to be, I hope, establishing some task and finish groups to look at how exactly this can work. But we want a system that is more person centred, that's more accessible, that's more trauma informed, so that children don't have to keep retraumatising themselves by disclosing time and again about the same thing. We need to make sure that how the system itself is experienced improves and is made better, because of the voices of people who've gone through too many awful things in the past as well. As I said to Lynne, if there is one cornerstone in all of this structure, it is ensuring that children's voices and young people's voices, and adults at risk, that their voices shape structures and systems for the future. They will be central to all of this.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Natasha, am y cwestiynau hynny. Fel y dywedoch chi, mae'n rhaid i hyn fod yn ymwneud â gwneud gwelliannau i fywydau pobl. Ni all hyn ymwneud â'r hyn sydd i lawr ar ddarn o bapur yn unig, ni all ymwneud â'r hyn sy'n cael ei gasglu mewn graffiau yn unig. Mae'n ymwneud â ph'un a yw'r hyn sy'n cael ei gasglu yn cael ei ddadansoddi'n effeithiol, a yw'n arwain at weithredu ac a yw'r gweithredu hynny'n achub ac yn gwella bywydau pobl, oherwydd dyna'r pethau rydyn ni'n siarad amdanyn nhw yma. Felly, ni fydd yr un ohonom yn colli golwg ar hynny, wrth gwrs. Rydych chi wedi cyfeirio at achosion yn y gorffennol lle mae gormod o gyfleoedd a gollwyd wedi bod yn gyfleoedd lle gellid bod wedi gweithredu. Mae'n rhaid i ni ddysgu oddi wrthyn nhw. Mae'n rhaid i ni wneud popeth o fewn ein gallu i achub plant ac oedolion sy'n wynebu risg yn y dyfodol.

Ac, ydy, mae'r Llywodraeth hon wedi ymrwymo i gydymffurfio â'r gyfraith—bob amser, wrth gwrs. Ac rydyn ni hefyd wedi ymrwymo bob amser i amddiffyn y grwpiau hynny a'r bobl hynny sy'n wynebu'r risg fwyaf ac sy'n agored i niwed yn ein cymdeithas, ac mae sawl agwedd ar hyn. Mae hynny'n rhywbeth y mae'r Dirprwy Brif Weinidog bob amser wedi bod yn gyson arno.

O ran yr hyn y gwnaethoch chi ei ofyn am beth fydd hyn yn ei olygu i staff rheng flaen, wel, bydd hyn, wrth gwrs, yn golygu grymuso staff rheng flaen. Oherwydd bydd cymaint o gyfleoedd a gollwyd y bydd y staff eu hunain wedi'u nodi, pan allai staff gwahanol fod wedi gweld rhywbeth, boed hynny mewn un ardal neu'r un patrymau yn dod i'r amlwg mewn gwahanol leoedd. Bydd hyn yn golygu ein bod ni'n sicrhau bod lleisiau'r staff hynny yn cael eu clywed ac na fyddan nhw'n sefyll ar eu pennau eu hunain mwyach.

Ac, wrth gwrs, fel y soniais i wrth Claire, bydd yn rhaid i ni edrych ar hyfforddiant a gwneud yn siŵr bod staff, er mwyn cael eu grymuso, yn gallu defnyddio'r—. I wneud yn siŵr eu bod yn ymwybodol o sut mae hyn yn mynd i newid eu gwaith, ond mae'n ymwneud â'u grymuso a pheidio â rhoi beichiau pellach arnyn nhw. Oherwydd, wrth gwrs, mae llawer o hyn, o ran—. Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am gapasiti. Mae hyn yn ymarferol oherwydd dydy llawer iawn o hyn ddim yn creu rhwymedigaethau newydd; mae hyn yn ymwneud â phan fydd staff yn sylwi ar bethau, pan fydd staff yn gwneud eu gwaith, ein bod ni'n cael y darlun cenedlaethol hwnnw a bod gennym fwy o gydlyniant yn gyffredinol. Felly, dydy e ddim yn ymwneud â chreu ffurflenni newydd neu unrhyw beth fel yna y bydd angen i staff eu llenwi; mae'n ymwneud â sicrhau bod pob cyswllt yn cyfrif ac y gwrandewir ar bob llais.

Fe ofynnoch chi rai cwestiynau penodol ynglŷn â phryd, ac fe soniais i'n gynharach y bydd hon yn rhaglen waith fesul cam, fel y gallwn ni weithredu'n gyflym iawn ar y pethau y gallwn ni eu gwneud ar unwaith ac, ar yr un pryd, bwrw ymlaen â rhywfaint o'r gwaith sydd, fel y soniais i, yn mynd i gymryd mwy o amser ac ymgynghori pellach mewn rhai o'r meysydd hyn hefyd. O ran y bwrdd goruchwylio gweinidogol, y bwriad yw sefydlu hwnnw yn sicr erbyn dechrau'r flwyddyn nesaf.

O ran y cynllun diogelu cenedlaethol a'r gofrestr risg genedlaethol, mae'r ffrâm amser—. Felly, rwy'n credu ein bod ni wrthi'n penderfynu a fydd yn cwmpasu tair blynedd neu bum mlynedd, ond fe fydd yna bethau i'w cyflawni bob blwyddyn ac mae'n rhywbeth y byddwn ni'n gweithio arno dros y ddwy flynedd nesaf i'w sefydlu, o ran gwneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n gwybod sut olwg sydd ar system dda. Unwaith eto, mae hynny gyda'r gobaith o ymgynghori ar awdurdod amddiffyn oedolion a phlant yn y dyfodol. Felly, eto, mae hyn yn cael ei wneud yn raddol oherwydd dydyn ni ddim eisiau gwneud rhywbeth sydd wedyn yn mynd i—. Dydyn ni ddim eisiau colli'r hyn sy'n dda wrth gael gwared ar yr hyn sy'n wael. Felly, dyna pam—. Ac rwy'n gobeithio nad wyf wedi gofyn—.

Ac o ran sut yr eir ati i wrando ar leisiau plant, p'un a ydyn nhw'n mynd i fod yn bwysig yn y broses hon, fel y soniais i wrth Lynne, rydyn ni'n mynd i fod, rwy'n gobeithio, yn sefydlu rhai grwpiau gorchwyl a gorffen i edrych ar sut yn union y gall hyn weithio. Ond rydyn ni eisiau system sy'n canolbwyntio'n fwy ar yr unigolyn, sy'n fwy hygyrch, sy'n fwy ystyriol o drawma, fel nad oes rhaid i blant barhau i aildrawmateiddio eu hunain trwy ddatgelu dro ar ôl tro am yr un peth. Mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod y ffordd y mae'r system ei hun yn cael ei phrofi yn gwella ac yn cael ei wneud yn well, oherwydd lleisiau pobl sydd wedi mynd trwy ormod o bethau ofnadwy yn y gorffennol hefyd. Fel y dywedais i wrth Lynne, os oes un conglfaen yn yr holl strwythur hwn, y conglfaen hwnnw yw sicrhau bod lleisiau plant a lleisiau pobl ifanc, ac oedolion sy'n wynebu risg, bod eu lleisiau yn llunio strwythurau a systemau ar gyfer y dyfodol. Byddan nhw'n ganolog i hyn i gyd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
I declare an interest. My husband's a child protection social worker.

Five-year-old Logan Mwangi, two-year-old Lola James, 16-year-old Kaylea Titford, all three of them were here in Wales and had the attention of the local authorities, and all three sadly died. And the biggest single factor in the deaths of those children that was identified was lack of communication between the services.

I had been a child protection social worker for 25 years before I came into politics, and I cannot tell you how difficult and challenging it is to be a child protection social worker. It is so hard to do a job where you are, if you're doing a good job, listening to the child and the young person, and you are looking at all of the risks, and you bear the risks. I'm grateful to Natasha for mentioning—and I can't see it in your statement, but maybe it is something I haven't read—child protection social workers, because they are the critical front line in all of the changes you seek. You are looking at a wholesale, or the potential of a wholesale, reorganisation of this service.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Rwy'n datgan buddiant. Mae fy ngŵr yn weithiwr cymdeithasol amddiffyn plant.

Logan Mwangi, pum mlwydd oed, Lola James, dwy oed, Kaylea Titford, 16 oed, roedd y tri ohonyn nhw yma yng Nghymru ac yn cael sylw'r awdurdodau lleol, a bu farw'r tri. A'r ffactor unigol mwyaf a nodwyd ym marwolaethau'r plant hynny oedd diffyg cyfathrebu rhwng y gwasanaethau.

Roeddwn i wedi bod yn weithiwr cymdeithasol amddiffyn plant am 25 mlynedd cyn i mi ddod i mewn i wleidyddiaeth, ac ni allaf ddweud wrthych pa mor anodd a heriol yw hi i fod yn weithiwr cymdeithasol amddiffyn plant. Mae hi mor anodd gwneud swydd lle rydych chi, os ydych chi'n gwneud gwaith da, yn gwrando ar y plentyn a'r person ifanc, ac rydych chi'n edrych ar yr holl risgiau, ac rydych chi'n cario'r risgiau. Rwy'n ddiolchgar i Natasha am sôn am—a allaf i ddim ei weld yn eich datganiad, ond efallai ei fod yn rhywbeth nad wyf wedi'i ddarllen—weithwyr cymdeithasol amddiffyn plant, oherwydd nhw yw'r rheng flaen hanfodol yn yr holl newidiadau rydych chi'n ceisio. Rydych chi'n edrych ar ad-drefnu'r gwasanaeth hwn yn llwyr, neu'r posibilrwydd o wneud hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Thank you so much for your expertise and your work for many years in this area. You mentioned at the start that there are too many children who have been let down by our system in the past, and the workforce and people like your husband, people who are working day in, day out to protect them, and to save more children's lives must be commended, and that has to be central. Child protection social workers, of course, are going to be central in all of this.

What you've talked about there as well, in terms of ensuring that we work with children, that we learn from their voices, but also the voices of the people who support them. That has to be absolutely central to our approach. We're going to be working, of course, with lots of different partners, with the National Youth Advocacy Service, with Llamau, to make sure that we are learning every lesson possible and that there are no gaps in what we're doing.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch yn fawr iawn am eich arbenigedd a'ch gwaith am flynyddoedd lawer yn y maes hwn. Fe wnaethoch chi sôn ar y dechrau bod gormod o blant sydd wedi cael eu siomi gan ein system yn y gorffennol, ac mae'n rhaid canmol y gweithlu a phobl fel eich gŵr, pobl sy'n gweithio o ddydd i ddydd i'w hamddiffyn, ac i achub mwy o fywydau plant, ac mae'n rhaid i hynny fod yn ganolog. Mae gweithwyr cymdeithasol amddiffyn plant, wrth gwrs, yn mynd i fod yn ganolog yn hyn i gyd.

Yr hyn rydych chi wedi sôn amdano yn y fan yna hefyd, o ran sicrhau ein bod ni'n gweithio gyda phlant, ein bod ni'n dysgu o'u lleisiau nhw, ond lleisiau'r bobl sy'n eu cefnogi hefyd. Mae'n rhaid i hynny fod yn hollol ganolog i'n dull gweithredu. Rydyn ni'n mynd i fod yn gweithio, wrth gwrs, gyda llawer o bartneriaid gwahanol, gyda'r Gwasanaeth Eiriolaeth Ieuenctid Cenedlaethol, gyda Llamau, i wneud yn siŵr ein bod ni'n dysgu pob gwers bosibl ac nad oes unrhyw fylchau yn yr hyn rydyn ni'n ei wneud.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I very much welcome the emphasis on a whole-system approach to safeguarding, and the ambition to strengthen the system's capacity for early identification and intervention, moving us away from a predominantly reactive model towards one that is genuinely preventative and intelligence led. I want to focus on design principles, which you've mentioned already, particularly on the commitment that the voices of children, young people, adults at risk, victims and survivors will be central to service design. As you've said, centring lived experience at the heart of safeguarding means that experiences should actively inform the systems and practices designed to protect children, and organisations should be able to demonstrate what has changed as a result. This is where there can be a danger of coming up short, because listening can feel like an achievement in and of itself, as opposed to a basis for action. So, how will the Government ensure this doesn't become the case? Like Natasha Asghar and Lynne Neagle, I wanted to ask you about how children, young people, adults at risk, victims and survivors will be engaged in the development and design of safeguarding services. Now, whilst you've answered that question, I'd also like to know—
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Rwy'n croesawu'n fawr y pwyslais ar ddull system gyfan o ddiogelu, a'r uchelgais i gryfhau gallu'r system i adnabod ac ymyrryd yn gynnar, gan ein symud i ffwrdd o fodel adweithiol yn bennaf tuag at un sy'n wirioneddol ataliol ac yn cael ei arwain gan wybodaeth. Rwyf am ganolbwyntio ar egwyddorion dylunio, yr ydych wedi sôn amdanyn nhw eisoes, yn enwedig ar yr ymrwymiad y bydd lleisiau plant, pobl ifanc, oedolion sy'n wynebu risg, dioddefwyr a goroeswyr yn ganolog i ddyluniad gwasanaethau. Fel y dywedoch chi, mae gosod profiad bywyd wrth wraidd diogelu yn golygu y dylai profiadau lywio'r systemau a'r arferion sydd wedi'u cynllunio i amddiffyn plant, a dylai sefydliadau allu dangos beth sydd wedi newid o ganlyniad. Dyma lle gall fod perygl o beidio â chyrraedd y nod, oherwydd gall gwrando deimlo fel cyflawniad ynddo'i hun, yn hytrach na sail i weithredu. Felly, sut fydd y Llywodraeth yn sicrhau na fydd hyn yn digwydd? Fel Natasha Asghar a Lynne Neagle, roeddwn i eisiau gofyn i chi sut y bydd plant, pobl ifanc, oedolion sy'n wynebu risg, dioddefwyr a goroeswyr yn cymryd rhan yn y gwaith o ddatblygu a dylunio gwasanaethau diogelu. Nawr, er eich bod chi wedi ateb y cwestiwn hwnnw, hoffwn i wybod hefyd—

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Sera, and, as you said, listening alone cannot be enough. And the point has been made by Members across the Chamber that the measure of success is going to be where the children and young people and adults at risk and victims and survivors can see that their experiences have influenced decisions, have improved practice and that they lead to better outcomes. That is the measure of success here. And, of course, we want to make sure that lived experience goes further in influencing policy and that organisations, again, not only listen but demonstrate what they've done differently as a result. And the ministerial group will want a clear line of sight of this.

You asked about overall scrutiny. There will be a really clear role for that in terms of internal to Government. I will be very interested to see what the Senedd proposes as well in terms of scrutinising this, because that will be of vital importance as well.

A number of Members have asked for some practical examples about how this is going to help children and young people at risk. Maybe one example: safeguarding systems can be very difficult to understand and to navigate, and national programme materials could maybe, perhaps, help individuals to understand the safeguarding system. They could be shaped by the voices of those who have used these services in the past, so that children and young people would not have to be seeing this through the lens of something as frightening—that they would be seeing it shaped by children and young people who have gone through it themselves. But, again, all of these ideas are to be developed by that expertise. So, diolch, Sera.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Sera, ac, fel y dywedoch chi, ni all gwrando ar ei ben ei hun fod yn ddigon. Ac mae Aelodau ar draws y Siambr wedi gwneud y pwynt mai'r mesur o lwyddiant fydd lle gall y plant a'r bobl ifanc a'r oedolion sy'n wynebu risg a'r dioddefwyr a'r goroeswyr weld bod eu profiadau wedi dylanwadu ar benderfyniadau, wedi gwella ymarfer a'u bod yn arwain at ganlyniadau gwell. Dyna'r mesur o lwyddiant yn y fan yma. Ac, wrth gwrs, rydyn ni eisiau gwneud yn siŵr bod profiad bywyd yn mynd ymhellach wrth ddylanwadu ar bolisi a bod sefydliadau, unwaith eto, nid yn unig yn gwrando ond yn dangos beth maen nhw wedi'i wneud yn wahanol o ganlyniad. A bydd y grŵp gweinidogol eisiau golwg glir ar hyn.

Fe wnaethoch chi ofyn am graffu yn gyffredinol. Bydd yna rôl glir iawn i hynny o ran mewnol i'r Llywodraeth. Bydd gen i ddiddordeb mawr i weld beth fydd y Senedd yn ei gynnig hefyd o ran craffu ar hyn, oherwydd bydd hynny'n hanfodol bwysig hefyd.

Mae nifer o Aelodau wedi gofyn am rai enghreifftiau ymarferol i ddangos sut mae hyn yn mynd i helpu plant a phobl ifanc sy'n wynebu risg. Efallai un enghraifft: gall systemau diogelu fod yn anodd iawn eu deall a'u llywio, ac efallai y gallai deunyddiau rhaglen genedlaethol helpu unigolion i ddeall y system ddiogelu. Gallent gael eu llunio gan leisiau'r rhai sydd wedi defnyddio'r gwasanaethau hyn yn y gorffennol, fel na fyddai plant a phobl ifanc yn gorfod gweld hyn trwy lens rhywbeth mor frawychus—y bydden nhw'n ei weld yn cael ei lunio gan blant a phobl ifanc sydd wedi mynd trwyddo eu hunain. Ond, unwaith eto, bydd yr holl syniadau hyn yn cael eu datblygu gan yr arbenigedd hwnnw. Felly, diolch, Sera.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Deputy Llywydd. To declare an interest, I've got a close family member working in the NHS.

Deputy Minister, nobody disputes the importance of safeguarding. No-one disputes that children need to be safe from neglect, harm or abuse, and in that way, the statement's right. But we have to be realistic about what is happening on the ground in Wales. Across Wales, we have more than 7,000 looked-after children, around 4,800 living in foster placement, yet Wales needs 550 new foster carers every year. And at a time when the numbers of foster carers are declining, demands continue to rise. In Wales, more than 20 per cent of foster parents who left cited safeguarding allegations as the reason.

We also hear of too many cases of individuals in fostering, education, care and other professions spending months or years under safeguarding investigations. They can't move on with their lives, despite no wrongdoing ever being proven. Doctors face triple jeopardy: investigated by the police, the General Medical Council and the trust all at the same time as trying to work, if they're not off with stress. Nearly one in three who experience fitness-to-practice investigations experience suicidal thoughts, and sometimes investigations go on for years.

Does the Minister accept that safeguarding systems must protect the vulnerable, but must also be proportionate, timely and fair to those who are accused? As you say in the statement, we owe it to them to get this right.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Ddirprwy Lywydd. I ddatgan buddiant, mae gen i aelod agos o'r teulu sy'n gweithio yn y GIG.

Ddirprwy Weinidog, does neb yn amau pwysigrwydd diogelu. Nid oes neb yn amau bod angen i blant fod yn ddiogel rhag esgeulustod, niwed neu gamdriniaeth, ac yn y modd hwnnw, mae'r datganiad yn iawn. Ond mae'n rhaid i ni fod yn realistig ynglŷn â'r hyn sy'n digwydd ar lawr gwlad yng Nghymru. Ledled Cymru, mae gennym fwy na 7,000 o blant sy'n derbyn gofal, tua 4,800 yn byw mewn lleoliad maeth, ond mae angen 550 o ofalwyr maeth newydd ar Gymru bob blwyddyn. Ac ar adeg pan fo nifer y gofalwyr maeth yn gostwng, mae'r galwadau yn parhau i godi. Yng Nghymru, dywedodd mwy nag 20 y cant o rieni maeth a adawodd mai honiadau diogelu oedd y rheswm.

Rydym hefyd yn clywed am ormod o achosion o unigolion mewn maeth, addysg, gofal a phroffesiynau eraill yn treulio misoedd neu flynyddoedd o dan ymchwiliadau diogelu. Ni allant symud ymlaen gyda'u bywydau, er nad oes unrhyw gamwedd erioed wedi'i brofi. Mae meddygon yn wynebu perygl triphlyg: ymchwiliad gan yr heddlu, y Cyngor Meddygol Cyffredinol a'r ymddiriedolaeth i gyd ar yr un pryd â cheisio gweithio, os nad ydyn nhw i ffwrdd oherwydd straen. Mae bron i un o bob tri sy'n profi ymchwiliadau addasrwydd i ymarfer yn profi teimladau hunanladdol, ac weithiau mae ymchwiliadau'n mynd ymlaen am flynyddoedd.

A yw'r Gweinidog yn derbyn bod yn rhaid i systemau diogelu amddiffyn y rhai sy'n agored i niwed, ond rhaid iddynt hefyd fod yn gymesur, amserol a theg i'r rhai sy'n cael eu cyhuddo? Fel y dywedwch yn y datganiad, mae'n rhaid i ni gael hyn yn iawn er eu mwyn nhw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 5. Datganiad gan y Dirprwy Weinidog dros Ofal Cymdeithasol, Iechyd Meddwl ac Iechyd Menywod: Diogelu Cryfach ar gyfer Cymru Fwy Diogel
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 5. Statement by the Deputy Minister for Social Care, Mental Health and Women’s Health: Stronger Safeguarding for a Safer Wales
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Catherine, and it's a similar point, of course, that was raised by your colleague Claire, and of course that needs consideration to make sure that we don't have unintended consequences, and I do take that point, of course. The central, fundamental need here is for children's safety and the safety of individuals who are at risk to be at the centre of all of this. The intention here very much is that it will be further empowering those people who surround those children, and certainly not the opposite, which are the instances that you would have alluded to there.

That is why the system will be iterative, why it will build with time to make sure that we are spotting any potential negative consequences that we would never want to happen. And again, if any Members have concerns about things that you would like officials and for me to be considering in greater depth, then please, if you could write to me, I would be very grateful. Thank you for raising that. Diolch, Llywydd.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Catherine, ac mae'n bwynt tebyg, wrth gwrs, i'r un a godwyd gan eich cyd-Aelod Claire, ac wrth gwrs mae angen ystyried hynny i wneud yn siŵr nad ydym yn cael canlyniadau anfwriadol, ac rwy'n cymryd y pwynt hwnnw, wrth gwrs. Yr angen canolog, sylfaenol yma yw i ddiogelwch plant a diogelwch unigolion sydd mewn perygl fod wrth wraidd hyn i gyd. Y bwriad yma yw y bydd yn grymuso ymhellach y bobl hynny sy'n amgylchynu'r plant hynny, ac yn sicr nid i'r gwrthwyneb, sef yr enghreifftiau y byddech wedi cyfeirio atynt yna.

Dyna pam y bydd y system yn ailadroddus, pam y bydd yn adeiladu gydag amser i wneud yn siŵr ein bod yn sylwi ar unrhyw ganlyniadau negyddol posibl na fyddem byth eisiau iddyn nhw ddigwydd. Ac eto, os oes gan unrhyw Aelodau bryderon am bethau yr hoffech i swyddogion ac i mi fod yn eu hystyried yn fwy manwl, yna os gwelwch yn dda, os gwnewch chi ysgrifennu ataf, byddwn yn ddiolchgar iawn. Diolch am godi hynny. Diolch, Lywydd.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Cynnig NDM9307 Heledd Fychan, Lynne Neagle

Cynnig bod y Senedd:

1. Yn galw ar Lywodraeth Cymru a Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig i gydweithio i:

a) gwella hyblygrwydd cyllidol Llywodraeth Cymru, gan gynnwys dileu'r holl gyfyngiadau ar Gronfa Wrth Gefn Cymru;

b) adolygu’r ffordd y mae Fformiwla Barnett yn gweithredu er mwyn cael mwy o degwch a thryloywder; ac

c) ailddatgan y gefnogaeth i'r ymrwymiad o £14 biliwn ar gyfer seilwaith rheilffyrdd yng Nghymru a chyflymu’r gwaith cyflawni a sicrhau cyllid digonol ar gyfer prosiectau gwella ledled Cymru yn ystod cyfnod yr adolygiad gwariant cyfredol.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Motion NDM9307 Heledd Fychan, Lynne Neagle

To propose that the Senedd:

1. Calls on the Welsh and UK Governments to work together to:

a) enhance the Welsh Government’s fiscal flexibilities, including removal of all restrictions on the Wales Reserve;

b) review the operation of the Barnett Formula to strengthen fairness and transparency; and

c) reaffirm support for the commitment of £14 billion for rail infrastructure in Wales and accelerate delivery and sufficient funding for improvement projects across Wales during the current spending review period.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Lywydd, dwi'n cyflwyno'r cynnig gerbron y Senedd y prynhawn yma, ac mae'r ddadl hon yn ymwneud ag un egwyddor syml: sicrhau bod gan Gymru'r cyllid, yr hyblygrwydd cyllidol a'r buddsoddiad sydd eu hangen i ddelifro ar gyfer cymunedau ledled y wlad, i bob postcode. Rwy'n falch bod y cynnig hwn wedi'i gyflwyno ar y cyd â Llafur Cymru, sy'n adlewyrchu ymrwymiad cyffredin i sicrhau setliad cyllido teg i Gymru ac yn adeiladu ar waith y Llywodraeth flaenorol yn y maes hwn. Mae'r materion hyn yn effeithio ar gymunedau ledled Cymru, ac rwy'n gobeithio gall fod consensws eang ar draws y Senedd y prynhawn yma ar bwysigrwydd y materion yma.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Llywydd, I move the motion before the Senedd this afternoon, and this debate is about one simple principle: ensuring that Wales has the funding, the fiscal flexibility and the investment required to deliver for communities across the country, for every postcode. I am pleased that this motion has been jointly tabled with Welsh Labour, which reflects a shared commitment to securing a fair funding settlement for Wales and builds on the work of the previous Government in this area. These issues affect communities across Wales, and I hope that there can be broad consensus across the Senedd this afternoon on the importance of these issues.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Mae'r cynnig yn galw ar Lywodraethau Cymru a'r Deyrnas Gyfunol i weithio gyda'n gilydd mewn tri maes allweddol: i wella hyblygrwydd cyllidol Cymru, i adolygu gweithrediad fformiwla Barnett ac i ailddatgan cefnogaeth i ymrwymiad Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol i fuddsoddi £14 biliwn mewn seilwaith rheilffyrdd ledled Cymru. Mae'r rhain yn gamau ymarferol, cyraeddadwy a all helpu i gryfhau ein heconomi, cefnogi gwasanaethau cyhoeddus a gwella bywydau pobl. Nid ydynt yn geisiadau am driniaeth arbennig. Maent yn geisiadau am ddull cydweithredol a fydd yn arwain at ganlyniadau gwell i Gymru.

Hyblygrwydd cyllidol, felly. Mae'r Prif Weinidog wedi bod yn glir bod Llywodraeth Cymru yn wynebu rhagolygon ariannol eithriadol o heriol, gyda disgwyl i gyllideb y flwyddyn nesaf fod yn is mewn termau real nag eleni. Tra bo'r galw ar ein gwasanaethau cyhoeddus, ein seilwaith a'n heconomi yn parhau i gynyddu, nid yw'r cyllid sydd ar gael inni yn cadw cam â hyn. Mae'r rhagolygon cyfredol yn dangos gostyngiad termau real yn ein cyllideb adnodd o 0.7 y cant yn ystod 2027-28, tra bod disgwyl i'r gyllideb gyfalaf fod tua 9 y cant yn is mewn termau real erbyn diwedd cyfnod yr adolygiad gwariant yn 2030.

Gallai'r her hon ddod yn fwy fyth unwaith y bydd goblygiadau cyhoeddiadau diweddar Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol ar wariant amddiffyn yn gliriach i ni. Yn yr amgylchiadau hyn, mae'n bwysicach nag erioed bod gan Gymru gyllid teg, y pwerau cyllidol a'r hyblygrwydd sydd eu hangen i gwrdd â heriau, buddsoddi yn ein blaenoriaethau a chyflawni ar gyfer cymunedau. Mae sicrhau bod gan Gymru'r offer i reoli ei chyllid ei hun yn effeithiol yn hanfodol er mwyn i benderfyniadau am Gymru adlewyrchu anghenion a blaenoriaethau Cymru. 

Gall cyhoeddiadau yn ystod y flwyddyn gan Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol, newidiadau i broffiliau gwariant ac amgylchiadau economaidd annisgwyl oll gael effaith sylweddol ar ein gwaith o gynllunio'r gyllideb. Ond o dan y trefniadau presennol, dim ond mynediad cyfyngedig i'n cronfa wrth gefn sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru a hyblygrwydd cyllidol mwy cyfyngedig na rhannau eraill o'r Deyrnas Gyfunol. Bu'n rhaid i Lywodraeth Cymru ofyn am hepgoriadau dros dro i gyfyngiadau'r cronfa wrth gefn mewn tair o'r pedair blynedd ddiwethaf. Nid yw hynny'n ffordd effeithiol o reoli cyllid cyhoeddus. Ni ddylem orfod gofyn i Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol bob blwyddyn am yr hyblygrwydd sydd eisoes ar gael mewn rhannau eraill o'r Deyrnas Unedig. Felly, rwy'n ceisio rhoi'r trefniadau dros dro hyn, y bu'n rhaid dibynnu arnynt dro ar ôl tro, ar sail barhaol, gan ddarparu mwy o sicrwydd a chefnogi gwaith effeithiol o gynllunio'r gyllideb.

Mae dileu'r cyfyngiadau ar gronfa wrth gefn Cymru yn gam cyntaf ymarferol. Byddai hynny'n caniatáu i Gymru wneud gwell defnydd o adnoddau sydd eisoes yn perthyn i Gymru ac yn dod â'n trefniadau yn nes at y rhai sydd ar gael yn yr Alban. Heb fynediad llawn at gronfa wrth gefn, dim ond £200 miliwn y byddaf i'n gallu ei thynnu i lawr, sef ymhell o dan 1 y cant o gyllideb Cymru, er mwyn helpu i ymdrin â phwysau y gwyddom amdanynt eisoes a phwysau sy'n dod i'r amlwg. Mae hyn yn cynnwys effeithiau cyhoeddiadau ariannu Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Gyfunol o fewn blwyddyn, megis y toriadau disgwyliedig i'n setliad cyfalaf o ganlyniad i gynnydd mewn gwariant ar amddiffyn.

Wrth gwrs, mae'r materion yn ymestyn y tu hwnt i weithrediad cronfa wrth gefn Cymru yn unig. Mae'r achos dros fwy o hyblygrwydd yn tynnu sylw at gwestiwn ehangach ynghylch a yw trefniadau cyllidol Cymru yn parhau i fod yn addas. Dyna pam yr wyf yn cynnig adolygiad o fframwaith cyllidol Cymru. Mae degawd wedi mynd heibio ers i'r fframwaith cyllidol gael ei gytuno yn 2016. Mae Cymru wedi newid. Mae'r amgylchedd economaidd wedi newid. Mae'r dirwedd gyfansoddiadol wedi newid. Mae'n rhesymol gofyn a yw'r trefniadau presennol yn parhau i fod yn addas i'r diben ac a ydynt yn rhoi'r gwytnwch a'r hyblygrwydd sydd eu hangen i Gymru i gwrdd â heriau yn y dyfodol. 

Fel rhan o'r adolygiad, byddaf eisiau mynd i'r afael ag amrywiaeth o faterion, gan gynnwys gweithrediad a hyblygrwydd cronfa wrth gefn Cymru a digonolrwydd pwerau benthyca Cymru—a chofiwch fod gan awdurdodau lleol fwy o hyblygrwydd cyllidol nag sydd gan Lywodraeth Cymru. Hefyd mae angen edrych ar effeithiolrwydd y trefniadau cyllido presennol o ran adlewyrchu angen cymharol a'r achos dros ddatganoli treth pellach. Mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn bwriadu ceisio datganoli pwerau pellach dros dreth incwm, ynghyd â datganoli'r doll teithwyr awyr. Byddwn hefyd yn ceisio cymhwysedd deddfwriaethol ar wahân ar gyfer treth newydd ar dir gwag.

Mae'r materion hyn yn mynd y tu hwnt i'r cynnig sydd gerbron y Senedd heddiw, ond gallaf roi'r ymrwymiad hwn ichi heddiw: ni fyddaf yn cytuno, fel Gweinidog cyllid, i fframwaith cyllidol diwygiedig oni bai ei fod yn gynnig da i Gymru, a bydd barn y Senedd yma ar hynny yn ystyriaeth bwysig wrth i’r adolygiad fynd yn ei flaen.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
The motion calls on the Welsh and UK Governments to work together in three key areas: enhancing Wales's fiscal flexibilities, to review the operation of the Barnett formula and to reaffirm support for the UK Government's commitment to invest £14 billion in rail infrastructure across Wales. These are practical, achievable steps that can help to strengthen our economy, support public services and improve people's lives. They are not asks for special treatment. They are asks for a collaborative approach to lead to better outcomes for Wales.

Fiscal flexibilities, therefore. The First Minister has been clear that the Welsh Government faces an exceptionally challenging financial outlook, with next year's budget expected to be lower in real terms than this year's. While demands on our public services, our infrastructure and economy continue to grow, the funding available to us is not keeping pace. Current forecasts point to a real-terms reduction in our resource budget of 0.7 per cent in 2027-28, while our capital budget is expected to be around 9 per cent lower in real terms by the end of the spending review period in 2030.

That challenge may become even greater once the implications of recent announcements by the UK Government on defence spending become clearer. In these circumstances, it's more important than ever that Wales has fair funding and the fiscal powers and flexibility needed to meet emerging challenges, invest in our priorities and deliver for communities across Wales. Ensuring that Wales has the tools to manage its own finances effectively is essential if decisions about Wales are to reflect Wales's needs and priorities.

In-year announcements from the UK Government, changing spending profiles and unforeseen economic circumstances can all have substantial impacts on our budget planning. But under current arrangements, the Welsh Government only has limited access to its own reserve and more restricted fiscal flexibilities than other parts of the UK. The Welsh Government has had to seek temporary waivers to Wales reserve restrictions in three of the last four years. That is not an effective way to manage public finances. We should not have to ask the UK Government each year for flexibilities that are already available elsewhere in the UK. I'm therefore seeking to place these temporary arrangements, which we have had to rely on repeatedly, on a permanent footing, providing greater certainty and supporting effective budget planning.

Removing restrictions on the Wales reserve is a practical first step. It would allow Wales to make better use of resources that already belong to Wales and bring our arrangements closer to those available in Scotland. Without full access to the Wales reserve, I will only be able to draw down £200 million, which is well under 1 per cent of the Wales budget, to assist with known and emerging pressures. This includes the impacts of funding announcements by the UK Government in year, such as the expected cuts in our capital settlement because of increased defence spending.

Of course, these issues extend beyond the operation of the Wales reserve alone. The case for greater flexibility highlights a broader question about whether Wales's fiscal arrangements remain fit for purpose. That's why I have proposed a review of the Wales fiscal framework. A decade has passed since the fiscal framework was agreed in 2016. Wales has changed. The economic environment has changed. The constitutional landscape has changed. It's reasonable to ask whether the current arrangements remain fit for purpose and whether they provide Wales with the resilience and flexibility required to meet future challenges.

As part of that review, I will be looking to address a variety of issues, including the operation and flexibility of the Wales reserve and the adequacy of Wales's borrowing powers—and remember that local authorities have greater flexibilities than the Welsh Government has. We also need to look at the effectiveness of current funding arrangements in reflecting relative need and the case for further tax devolution. The Welsh Government plans to seek further income tax devolution and the devolution of air passenger duty. We will also be separately seeking competence for a new vacant land tax.

These issues go beyond the motion before the Senedd today, but I can also give you this commitment today: I will not agree, as finance Minister, a revised fiscal framework unless it is a good deal for Wales, and the opinion of the Senedd on this will be an important consideration as the review proceeds.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
