XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Every local authority in Britain can move money into and out of reserves. This includes town and community councils and it actually includes school governing bodies, who can also move money into and out of reserves. No controls, no rules. It's their money, they can spend it or save it. Why is the Welsh Government treated differently? Once money is allocated to Wales or is raised in Wales, the Treasury has no legitimate interest in that money. This is the way they treat Westminster committees and how they treat different spending areas in Westminster. It is not the way to treat a Government.

Money is sometimes allocated late in the year, sometimes very late in the year. Money has been claimed back. There is an expectation it could have been carried forward, but that's only an expectation. The rules are really unfair. If not always able to carry it forward, money was claimed back. I did suggest at the time that we should not rely on the Treasury being fair—I don't think anybody's ever thought the Treasury was fair—and that we should actually take the money and spend it. We could give it to local authorities or give it to housing associations without any problem at all. But this is not a way to run a national budget. It does not cost the Treasury any money. Once it's here, it's here, and I don't see why they want to get involved in micromanaging Wales. It has to end. And once the money is allocated, then why does the Treasury want to get involved? It is not their money, they should be leaving us alone.

On funding, despite what has been said and believed, Wales does well out of the current system. We receive substantially more than we pay in. Estimates suggest that we collect about 70 per cent to 75 per cent of the per capita income in Wales. We spend about 110 per cent, including central Government expenditure, here in Wales. This is what being part of a larger country means—money is provided to those who need it most.

What should a funding system look like? Characteristics of a funding system for subnational Governments that were originally proposed by the Calman commission include: stability and predictability; simplicity and transparency; autonomy; efficiency; equity, so that resources are allocated in a way that takes account of relative need; and accountability, so that the link between decisions made and the tax paid by voters is clear. Any additional tax take within a region should impact on the budget available.

The Barnett formula evolved from the Goschen formula, which was designed specifically to preserve Scotland's public expenditure advantage over England. The formula was thus never designed with Wales in mind. Applied rigorously, the formula should have led to convergence in levels of spending per head across the UK. The formula has, however, preserved the spending advantage for Wales over England. There have been periodic adjustments to the operation of the formula since 1980, mainly through relative population changes. These adjustments have increased relative spending levels in Wales. The main advantage of the formula is its simplicity and objectivity as a basis for making spending allocations. There has been notable success in securing formula bypass since devolution. For example, Objective 1 match funding and funding for city deals. Northern Ireland has done substantially better in receiving money in excess of the Barnett formula. Remember, the Barnett formula calculates the minimum to be provided. Anything over and above that is allowed to be provided by the Government if they so desire.

We also have the Barnett floor. It was set following the Holtham commission investigation into the needs of Wales. At the 2015 spending review, the UK Conservative Government—see, Sam, I do mention the Conservatives—implemented a funding floor in Wales. This provided a guarantee that the Welsh Government block grant funding per head would not fall below 115 per cent of equivalent spending per head in England. Currently in Wales we get about 120 per cent of the equivalent funding per head in England. With the result of the Holtham review that Wales needs 115 per cent of the equivalent funding per head in England in devolved areas, if we get 120 per cent, we're doing well.

Currently, the total budget is £27.5 billion—£22.8 billion in revenue and £3.6 billion in capital. So, if Wales gets its 115 per cent, which is what Holtham said, then we get about £1 billion more than we should be getting, or than would be calculated. So, this idea that Wales is treated very badly by everybody might play well in certain circles, but it doesn't actually play with reality. This needs recalculating. I suggest academics, jointly appointed by the Welsh Government and the Treasury, at five-yearly intervals, should recalculate Wales's need. But remember, there's a danger that Wales will get less.

I support additional funding for rail. I have stations in my constituency that we need to be opening and reopening. Would money better be spent on transport in general? We need work doing on bus and rail interchanges. We need to ensure adequate parking near the new stations. What we do not need are rail lines to fulfil the wishes of the few passengers who want to use them.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Gall pob awdurdod lleol ym Mhrydain symud arian i mewn ac allan o gronfeydd wrth gefn. Mae hyn yn cynnwys cynghorau tref a chymuned ac mewn gwirionedd mae'n cynnwys cyrff llywodraethu ysgolion, a all hefyd symud arian i mewn ac allan o gronfeydd wrth gefn. Dim rheolaethau, dim rheolau. Eu harian nhw ydyw, fe allan nhw ei wario neu ei gynilo. Pam mae Llywodraeth Cymru yn cael ei thrin yn wahanol? Unwaith y bydd arian yn cael ei ddyrannu i Gymru neu yn cael ei godi yng Nghymru, nid oes gan y Trysorlys unrhyw ddiddordeb dilyn yn yr arian hwnnw. Dyma'r ffordd maen nhw'n trin pwyllgorau San Steffan a sut maen nhw'n trin gwahanol feysydd gwariant yn San Steffan. Nid dyma'r ffordd i drin Llywodraeth.

Mae arian weithiau'n cael ei ddyrannu yn hwyr yn y flwyddyn, weithiau yn hwyr iawn yn y flwyddyn. Mae arian wedi'i hawlio'n ôl. Mae disgwyliad y gellid bod wedi cael ei gario ymlaen, ond dim ond disgwyliad yw hynny. Mae'r rheolau'n annheg iawn. Os nad oedd bob amser modd ei gario ymlaen, hawliwyd arian yn ôl. Awgrymais ar y pryd na ddylem ni ddibynnu ar i'r Trysorlys fod yn deg—nid wyf yn credu bod unrhyw un erioed wedi meddwl bod y Trysorlys yn deg—ac y dylem ni gymryd yr arian a'i wario mewn gwirionedd. Fe allwn ni ei roi i awdurdodau lleol neu ei roi i gymdeithasau tai heb unrhyw broblem o gwbl. Ond nid yw hyn yn ffordd o redeg cyllideb genedlaethol. Nid yw'n costio unrhyw arian i'r Trysorlys. Unwaith y bydd yma, mae yma, a dydw i ddim yn gweld pam eu bod arnyn nhw eisiau mân-reoli Cymru. Mae'n rhaid iddo ddod i ben. Ac unwaith y bydd yr arian wedi'i ddyrannu, yna pam mae ar y Trysorlys eisiau ymyrryd? Nid eu harian nhw ydyw, fe ddylen nhw fod yn gadael llonydd inni.

O ran cyllid, er gwaethaf yr hyn sydd wedi'i ddweud a'i gredu, mae Cymru'n gwneud yn dda o'r system bresennol. Rydym ni'n derbyn llawer mwy na rydym ni'n talu. Mae amcangyfrifon yn awgrymu ein bod yn casglu tua 70 y cant i 75 y cant o'r incwm y pen yng Nghymru. Rydym ni'n gwario tua 110 y cant, gan gynnwys gwariant y Llywodraeth ganolog, yma yng Nghymru. Dyma beth mae bod yn rhan o wlad fwy yn ei olygu—darperir arian i'r rhai sydd ei angen fwyaf.

Sut ddylai system ariannu edrych? Mae nodweddion system ariannu ar gyfer Llywodraethau is-genedlaethol a gynigiwyd yn wreiddiol gan gomisiwn Calman yn cynnwys: sefydlogrwydd a rhagweladwyedd; symlrwydd a thryloywder; ymreolaeth; effeithlonrwydd; cydraddoldeb, fel bod adnoddau yn cael eu dyrannu mewn ffordd sy'n ystyried angen cymharol; ac atebolrwydd, fel bod y cysylltiad rhwng penderfyniadau a wneir a'r dreth a delir gan bleidleiswyr yn glir. Dylai unrhyw dreth ychwanegol o fewn rhanbarth effeithio ar y gyllideb sydd ar gael.

Esblygodd fformiwla Barnett o fformiwla Goschen, a gynlluniwyd yn benodol i gadw mantais gwariant cyhoeddus yr Alban dros Loegr. Felly ni chafodd y fformiwla erioed ei chynllunio gyda Chymru mewn golwg. Wedi'i gymhwyso'n drylwyr, dylai'r fformiwla fod wedi arwain at gydgyfeirio lefelau gwariant y pen ledled y Deyrnas Unedig. Mae'r fformiwla, fodd bynnag, wedi cadw'r fantais wariant i Gymru dros Loegr. Bu addasiadau achlysurol i weithrediad y fformiwla ers 1980, yn bennaf trwy newidiadau cymharol i'r boblogaeth. Mae'r addasiadau hyn wedi cynyddu lefelau gwariant cymharol yng Nghymru. Prif fantais y fformiwla yw ei symlrwydd a'i wrthrychedd fel sail ar gyfer gwneud dyraniadau gwariant. Bu llwyddiant nodedig wrth sicrhau ffyrdd o osgoi'r fformiwla ers datganoli. Er enghraifft, cyllid cyfatebol Amcan 1 a chyllid ar gyfer bargeinion dinesig. Mae Gogledd Iwerddon wedi gwneud yn sylweddol well wrth dderbyn arian sy'n fwy na fformiwla Barnett. Cofiwch, mae fformiwla Barnett yn cyfrifo'r lleiafswm i'w ddarparu. Gall y Llywodraeth ddarparu unrhyw beth dros hynny os yw hi'n dymuno.

Mae gennym ni lawr Barnett hefyd. Fe'i sefydlwyd yn dilyn ymchwiliad comisiwn Holtham i anghenion Cymru. Yn adolygiad gwariant 2015, gweithredodd Llywodraeth Geidwadol y Deyrnas Unedig—dyna chi, Sam, rwy'n sôn am y Ceidwadwyr—lawr cyllido yng Nghymru. Roedd hyn yn warant na fyddai cyllid grant bloc Llywodraeth Cymru y pen yn disgyn o dan 115 y cant o'r gwariant cyfatebol y pen yn Lloegr. Ar hyn o bryd yng Nghymru rydym ni'n cael tua 120 y cant o'r cyllid cyfatebol y pen yn Lloegr. Gyda chanlyniad adolygiad Holtham bod angen 115 y cant o'r cyllid cyfatebol y pen ar Gymru mewn ardaloedd datganoledig, os cawn ni 120 y cant, rydym ni'n gwneud yn dda.

Ar hyn o bryd, cyfanswm y gyllideb yw £27.5 biliwn—£22.8 biliwn mewn refeniw a £3.6 biliwn mewn cyfalaf. Felly, os yw Cymru'n cael ei 115 y cant, a dyna a ddywedodd Holtham, yna rydyn ni'n cael tua £1 biliwn yn fwy nag y dylem ni fod yn ei gael, neu nag y byddai'n cael ei gyfrifo. Felly, gallai'r syniad hwn bod Cymru yn cael ei thrin yn wael iawn gan bawb swnio'n dda mewn rhai cylchoedd, ond nid dyna'r gwirionedd. Mae angen ailgyfrifo hyn. Awgrymaf y dylai academyddion, a benodwyd ar y cyd gan Lywodraeth Cymru a'r Trysorlys, bob pum mlynedd, ailgyfrifo anghenion Cymru. Ond cofiwch, mae perygl y bydd Cymru'n cael llai.

Rwy'n cefnogi cyllid ychwanegol ar gyfer rheilffyrdd. Mae gen i orsafoedd yn fy etholaeth y mae angen i ni fod yn agor ac ailagor. A fyddai'n well gwario arian ar drafnidiaeth yn gyffredinol? Mae angen i ni wneud gwaith ar gyfnewidfeydd bysiau a rheilffyrdd. Mae angen i ni sicrhau parcio digonol ger y gorsafoedd newydd. Yr hyn nad oes ei angen arnom ni yw llinellau rheilffordd i gyflawni dymuniadau'r ychydig deithwyr sydd eisiau eu defnyddio.

Hoffwn roi ar y cofnod, i gychwyn, fy mod i wrth gwrs yn cefnogi pwynt 1 a phwynt 2 yn y cynnig sydd o'n blaenau. XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: I'm pleased to be able to contribute to this important debate this afternoon. I'd like to put on record at the outset that of course I support point 1 and point 2 in the motion before us. A number of my fellow Members on these benches have made the case clear again today as to why we need to see urgent action from the UK Government, and I wish to focus my comments on point 3 of the motion.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
When the Prime Minister, Keir Starmer, made his way to Wales to announce £14 billion of investment to, as he put it, 'transform' Welsh rail, I'm sure many of us were hopeful that it was signalling the beginning of the end of historic underfunding for Welsh rail. However, as the details of commitments emerged, it became clear that, far from putting Wales on the right track, this commitment risks facilitating the continuation of underinvestment in Welsh rail over the current spending review period. It also, of course, made no effort to right the wrongs of the HS2 and the Oxford and Cambridge lines scandal. And whilst I'm sure we are glad to hear the new Prime Minister recently confirm that the £14 billion commitment remains firmly in place, I would maybe suggest to the Labour Party that it should have a word with Stephen Kinnock, the Secretary of State for Wales, given his views on this, as he doesn't quite seem to be on the same page as you in the Labour Party here, or even the Prime Minister.

Point 3 in today's motion does not set out to give Wales any special treatment or to secure any additional funding. Rather, the motion aims to ensure that the UK Government's commitment properly aligns with the delivery timelines of projects in Wales that have already been given the green light.

As the Cabinet Minister for Finance put it in her letter to the Chancellor:

'At this level of funding, the projects underpinning the commitment cannot be progressed at the pace required and key commitments will not be delivered within the planned timeframe.'

If we continue as we are, deadlines will be missed, projects will be in limbo, jobs could be at risk, and rail in Wales will continue to lag behind the rest of the UK. I therefore urge you all to support this motion today.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Pan wnaeth y Prif Weinidog, Keir Starmer, ei ffordd i Gymru i gyhoeddi £14 biliwn o fuddsoddiad i, fel y dywedodd, 'drawsnewid' rheilffyrdd Cymru, rwy'n siŵr bod llawer ohonom ni'n gobeithio ei fod yn arwydd o ddechrau diwedd tanariannu hanesyddol ar gyfer rheilffyrdd Cymru. Fodd bynnag, wrth i fanylion yr ymrwymiadau ddod i'r amlwg, daeth yn amlwg, ymhell o roi Cymru ar y trywydd iawn, bod yr ymrwymiad hwn mewn perygl o hwyluso parhau i danfuddsoddi mewn rheilffyrdd Cymru dros y cyfnod adolygu gwariant presennol. Nid oedd hefyd, wrth gwrs, yn gwneud unrhyw ymdrech i gywiro camgymeriadau'r HS2 a sgandal llinellau Rhydychen a Chaergrawnt. Ac er fy mod i'n siŵr ein bod yn falch o glywed y Prif Weinidog newydd yn cadarnhau yn ddiweddar bod yr ymrwymiad o £14 biliwn yn parhau, efallai y byddwn yn awgrymu i'r Blaid Lafur y dylai gael gair gyda Stephen Kinnock, Ysgrifennydd Gwladol Cymru, o ystyried ei farn ar hyn, gan nad yw'n ymddangos ei fod o'r un farn â chi yn y Blaid Lafur yma, neu hyd yn oed y Prif Weinidog.

Nid yw pwynt 3 yn y cynnig heddiw yn bwriadu rhoi unrhyw driniaeth arbennig i Gymru na sicrhau unrhyw gyllid ychwanegol. Yn hytrach, nod y cynnig yw sicrhau bod ymrwymiad Llywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig yn cyd-fynd yn briodol ag amserlenni cyflawni prosiectau yng Nghymru sydd eisoes wedi cael sêl bendith.

Fel y dywedodd Gweinidog Cyllid y Cabinet yn ei llythyr at y Canghellor:

'Gyda'r swm yma o gyllid, ni ellir bwrw ymlaen â'r prosiectau sy'n sail i'r ymrwymiad yn ddigon cyflym ac ni fydd ymrwymiadau allweddol yn cael eu cyflawni o fewn yr amserlen a gynlluniwyd.'

Os byddwn yn parhau fel yr ydym ni, bydd dyddiadau cau yn cael eu methu, bydd prosiectau mewn rhyw dir neb, gallai swyddi fod mewn perygl, a bydd rheilffyrdd yng Nghymru yn parhau i fod ar ôl gweddill y Deyrnas Unedig. Felly, rwy'n eich annog chi i gyd i gefnogi'r cynnig hwn heddiw.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Devolution should never mean a transfer of responsibility without the means to discharge it, and yet, too often in Wales, we've been given the powers we have so far without the funds to use them, trying to meet our responsibilities with one hand tied behind our backs, and that erodes public confidence in devolution.

I welcome this debate. It has shown me, actually, that there is a significant amount of cross-party support for the three points in the motion. Just to touch on them very quickly, the Wales reserve: if a Government does not need to spend money in one year, it should be able to save it for what is needed in the next year. That's exactly how we all do our own budgets at home. If we don't spend it, we can carry it over, and, therefore, that should be the same application to our budget here in Wales. Scotland does not face the same constraints. It has unlimited annual drawdowns from its own reserve.

The need for flexibility, though, goes beyond the reserve. Last July, Members across this Senedd agreed that it makes little sense for a national Government to have less borrowing flexibility than a local council, as has been raised by Mike Hedges. We remain stuck, with an overall capital borrowing cap whose real value is eroded by inflation over the past decade.

Secondly, the Crown Estate. Borrowing and revenue have to go hand in hand. Wales has a revenue stream in sight, and, at the moment, it is being collected elsewhere. The Crown Estate's Welsh assets were valued at £853 million in 2022-23, and 93 per cent of that is tied to offshore wind and marine energy. Of course, devolving that revenue would come with a reduction in the block grant—we do know that. But, just as in Scotland, the way that adjustment is calculated matters. If it is set transparently and reflects the growth of offshore wind in Wales, it could give us the much-needed means to invest in our own coastline and communities.

On the Barnett formula, I welcome the motion's language of review, fairness and transparency. But we must, as has been said, be cautious, as the Institute for Fiscal Studies has noted. Reopening the formula could cost Wales as readily as it benefits. So, the credible route is not a leap in the dark; it is, as has been said, a rigorous, evidence-based process. At present, the Treasury acts as judge, jury and executioner in disputes. We've seen that HS2 is the clearest example, and the Oxford to Cambridge line as well. When the same decision goes against Wales twice and no-one outside the Treasury can overturn it, that is not an error, it is a flaw in the design. What we need is an independent fiscal commission, along the lines of Australia's Commonwealth Grants Commission.

Finally, on rail, I welcome the commitment to £14 billion-worth of investment, and I support, of course, devolving rail infrastructure to Wales, as Scotland has. I have to refer us to the modicum of confusion that there was in the last Senedd over the £14 billion and the befuddlement and confusion in terms of the motions coming forward to us. But let's move on from that, as we should see, in terms of our railways. We need to see that rail devolution come to Wales, with the money attached to it, and we need to make sure that that affects the whole of Wales.

To finish, I ask the Welsh Government to be bolder in what it asks for, and I ask the UK Government, in turn, to give us a fair hearing into a fair settlement. Diolch yn fawr iawn.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Ni ddylai datganoli byth olygu trosglwyddo cyfrifoldeb heb y modd i'w gyflawni, ac eto, yn rhy aml yng Nghymru, rydym ni wedi cael y pwerau sydd gennym ni hyd yma heb yr arian i'w defnyddio, gan geisio cyflawni ein cyfrifoldebau gydag un llaw wedi'i glymu y tu ôl i'n cefnau, ac mae hynny'n erydu hyder y cyhoedd mewn datganoli.

Rwy'n croesawu'r ddadl hon. Mae wedi dangos i mi, mewn gwirionedd, fod yna lawer iawn o gefnogaeth drawsbleidiol i'r tri phwynt yn y cynnig. Dim ond i'w crybwyll nhw'n gyflym iawn, cronfa wrth gefn Cymru: os nad oes angen i Lywodraeth wario arian mewn blwyddyn, dylai allu ei gynilo ar gyfer yr hyn sydd ei angen yn y flwyddyn nesaf. Dyna'n union sut rydym ni i gyd yn gwneud ein cyllidebau ein hunain gartref. Os nad ydym ni'n ei wario, fe allwn ni ei gario drosodd, ac, felly, dylai hynny fod yr un mor wir i'n cyllideb ni yma yng Nghymru. Nid yw'r Alban yn wynebu'r un cyfyngiadau. Fe all hi droi'n ddi-derfyn at ei chronfa wrth gefn ei hun.

Mae'r angen am hyblygrwydd, fodd bynnag, yn mynd y tu hwnt i'r gronfa wrth gefn. Ym mis Gorffennaf diwethaf, cytunodd Aelodau ar draws y Senedd hon nad yw'n gwneud llawer o synnwyr i Lywodraeth genedlaethol gael llai o hyblygrwydd benthyca na chyngor lleol, fel y soniodd Mike Hedges. Rydym ni'n parhau i fod yn sownd, gydag uchafswm benthyca cyfalaf cyffredinol y mae ei werth gwirioneddol wedi ei erydu gan chwyddiant dros y degawd diwethaf.

Yn ail, Ystad y Goron. Rhaid i fenthyca a refeniw fynd law yn llaw. Mae gan Gymru ffrwd refeniw posib, ac, ar hyn o bryd, mae'n cael ei gasglu mewn mannau eraill. Roedd asedau Cymreig Ystâd y Goron yn werth £853 miliwn yn 2022-23, ac mae 93 y cant o hynny'n gysylltiedig â ffermydd gwynt ar y môr ac ynni'r môr. Wrth gwrs, byddai datganoli'r refeniw hwnnw yn arwain at ostyngiad yn y grant bloc—rydyn ni'n gwybod hynny. Ond, yn union fel yn yr Alban, mae'r ffordd y mae'r addasiad hwnnw'n cael ei gyfrifo yn bwysig. Os caiff ei bennu'n dryloyw ac yn adlewyrchu twf ynni gwynt ar y môr yng Nghymru, gallai roi'r modd mawr ei angen i ni fuddsoddi yn ein harfordir a'n cymunedau ein hunain.

O ran fformiwla Barnett, rwy'n croesawu fel mae'r cynnig yn sôn am adolygu, tegwch a thryloywder. Ond mae'n rhaid i ni, fel y dywedwyd, fod yn ofalus, fel y mae'r Sefydliad Astudiaethau Cyllidol wedi nodi. Gallai ailagor y fformiwla olygu fod Cymru ar ei cholled, fel rŵan y mae hi ar ei hennill. Felly, nid y llwybr credadwy yw naid i'r tywyllwch; ond yn hytrach, fel y dywedwyd, proses drylwyr, sy'n seiliedig ar dystiolaeth. Ar hyn o bryd, mae'r Trysorlys yn gweithredu fel barnwr, rheithgor a dienyddiwr mewn anghydfodau. Rydym ni wedi gweld mai HS2 yw'r enghraifft gliriaf, a'r llinell Rhydychen i Gaergrawnt hefyd. Pan fydd yr un penderfyniad yn mynd yn erbyn Cymru ddwywaith a does neb y tu allan i'r Trysorlys yn gallu ei wyrdroi, nid yw hynny'n gamgymeriad, mae'n ddiffyg yn y dyluniad. Yr hyn sydd ei angen arnom mi yw comisiwn cyllidol annibynnol, rhywbeth tebyg i Gomisiwn Grantiau Cymanwlad Awstralia.

Yn olaf, o ran rheilffyrdd, rwy'n croesawu'r ymrwymiad i fuddsoddiad gwerth £14 biliwn, ac rwy'n cefnogi, wrth gwrs, datganoli'r seilwaith rheilffyrdd i Gymru, fel y mae'r Alban wedi. Mae'n rhaid i mi ein cyfeirio at y dryswch a fu yn y Senedd ddiwethaf dros y £14 biliwn a'r dryswch a'r penbleth o ran y cynigion a gyflwynwyd. Ond gadewch i ni symud ymlaen o hynny, fel y dylem ni weld, o ran ein rheilffyrdd. Mae angen i ni weld y datganolir rheilffyrdd i Gymru, gyda'r arian ynghlwm wrtho, ac mae angen i ni wneud yn siŵr bod hynny'n effeithio ar Gymru gyfan.

I orffen, gofynnaf i Lywodraeth Cymru fod yn fwy beiddgar yn yr hyn y mae'n gofyn amdano, ac rwy'n gofyn i Lywodraeth y Deyrnas Unedig, yn ei thro, roi gwrandawiad teg i ni a setliad teg. Diolch yn fawr iawn.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Galwaf yn awr ar y Gweinidog Cabinet i ymateb i'r ddadl.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
Diolch, Lywydd. To Reform, and to Cai Parry-Jones, may I start by saying that this Senedd most definitely should be discussing how we are funded? You tabled a debate last week on blankets of the past. I tabled one this week on the financing of Wales. Reform, you may be counting views and shares on social media. I'm counting the money made available and used in Wales. So, this motion is clear: it supports flexible access to reserves to enable better financial planning and control by Government, and that will definitely benefit the people of Wales.

Secondly, it supports better operation and transparency on the decisions that finance Wales via Barnett. These decisions should not be hidden behind a Treasury curtain. And it calls for rail investment in Wales to finally be realised, and those Burns stations, so often mentioned in this Senedd, to be built.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Diolch, Lywydd. I Reform, ac i Cai Parry-Jones, gaf i ddechrau trwy ddweud y dylai'r Senedd hon fod yn sicr yn trafod sut rydym yn cael ein hariannu? Fe wnaethoch chi gyflwyno dadl yr wythnos diwethaf ar flancedi o'r gorffennol. Fe wnes i gyflwyno un yr wythnos hon ar ariannu Cymru. Reform, efallai eich bod chi'n cyfrif faint o bobl sy'n gweld a rhannu pethau ar y cyfryngau cymdeithasol. Rydw i'n cyfrif yr arian sydd ar gael ac a ddefnyddir yng Nghymru. Felly, mae'r cynnig hwn yn glir: mae'n cefnogi mynediad hyblyg i gronfeydd wrth gefn i alluogi gwell cynllunio a rheolaeth ariannol gan y Llywodraeth, a bydd hynny'n bendant o fudd i bobl Cymru.

Yn ail, mae'n cefnogi gwell gweithrediad a thryloywder ar y penderfyniadau sy'n ariannu Cymru drwy Barnett. Ni ddylid cuddio'r penderfyniadau hyn y tu ôl i len y Trysorlys. Ac mae'n galw am wireddu buddsoddiad rheilffyrdd yng Nghymru o'r diwedd, ac adeiladu'r gorsafoedd Burns hynny, a grybwyllir mor aml yn y Senedd hon.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Felly, diolch i Lafur am gyd-gyflwyno’r cynnig a'r galwadau yma, a hefyd, yn y cyfraniad, am amlinellu'r ymrwymiad sydd gyda chi i ddiwygiad pellach ar gyllido Cymru. Fe amlinellodd Sera Evans hefyd yr angen am hyblygrwydd i'r mynediad yna ar gyfer ein cronfeydd wrth gefn ni, sydd mor bwysig i ni.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: So, I'd like to thank Labour for jointly tabling the motion and also for their contribution outlining the commitment that you have to further reform of the fiscal framework in Wales. Sera Evans also outlined the need for flexibility in that access to our reserves, which is so important to us.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Paul Marr, we share the same constituents, and I can tell you that they are interested in Wales getting its fair share of funding, and especially on rail investment in Pembrokeshire and into Aberystwyth. That's not ideology; that's better rail services.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Paul Marr, rydym ni'n rhannu'r un etholwyr, a gallaf ddweud wrthych chi fod ganddyn nhw ddiddordeb bod Cymru'n cael ei chyfran deg o gyllid, ac yn enwedig ar fuddsoddiad mewn rheilffyrdd yn sir Benfro ac i mewn i Aberystwyth. Nid ideoleg mo hynny; gwell gwasanaethau rheilffyrdd yw hynny.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Will you take a small intervention?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Wnewch chi dderbyn ymyriad byr?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: Yes.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Gwnaf.

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim: I'd just like to request, well, ask, really: do you appreciate that, if another funding review was to take place, it could actually result in Wales getting less funding? And if that was to happen, would you then accept that?
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated: Fe hoffwn i wneud cais, wel, gofyn, mewn gwirionedd: ydych chi'n sylweddoli, pe bai adolygiad cyllid arall, y gallai arwain at Gymru yn cael llai o arian? A phe digwyddai hynny, a fyddech chi'n derbyn hynny?

XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_welsh: 6. Dadl: Diwygio Cyllidol
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.Agenda_item_english: 6. Debate: Fiscal Reform
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_verbatim:
This motion today is not about the fiscal review; it's about the operation of Barnett. It is different to the call—.  It was seeking to create a consensus, a commonsense consensus, across this Chamber that you've decided that you don't sign up to.

It was good to hear the commonsense approach by the Conservatives, speaking of appropriate powers for appropriate use, and that's what good politics means. [Interruption.] Look at the detail of what's in front of you. Others have suggested and said quite clearly that we need to not lay on our laurels and remain just on what this motion today is seeking to create for the Senedd, but to be bolder—Jane Dodds's words; Carrie Harper also made that call.

I would say also, Mike Hedges, I will use that line when I next speak to the UK Treasury, when you reminded us all that school governing bodies and local authorities have more fiscal powers and borrowing powers than this Senedd itself has, on access to reserves in particular. You said the UK Treasury should not be micromanaging the finances of Wales, and that's a very important thing for us to get them to understand.

So, we've created a consensus here today. It doesn't include Reform. I won't lose any sleep over that. But if I can finish by just saying that these proposals in this motion are rooted in partnership, fairness and a shared cross-party ambition to improve outcomes for the people of Wales. And if that wasn't worth an hour of this Senedd's time, then I don't know what could be.
XML_Plenary_Bilingual.contribution_translated:
Nid yw'r cynnig hwn heddiw yn ymwneud â'r adolygiad cyllidol; mae'n ymwneud â sut mae Barnett yn gweithio. Mae'n wahanol i'r alwad—. Roedd yn ceisio creu consensws, consensws synnwyr cyffredin, ar draws y Siambr hon rydych chi wedi penderfynu nad ydych chi'n ei dderbyn.

Roedd yn dda clywed ymagwedd synnwyr cyffredin y Ceidwadwyr, yn siarad am bwerau priodol i'w defnyddio yn briodol, a dyna beth mae gwleidyddiaeth dda yn ei olygu. [Torri ar draws.] Edrychwch ar fanylion yr hyn sydd o'ch blaen. Mae eraill wedi awgrymu a dweud yn eithaf clir bod angen i ni beidio â gorffwys ar ein rhwyfau ac aros dim ond ar yr hyn y mae'r cynnig hwn heddiw yn ceisio ei greu i'r Senedd, ond i fod yn fwy beiddgar—geiriau Jane Dodds; fe alwodd Carrie Harper am hynny hefyd.

Byddwn yn dweud hefyd, Mike Hedges, byddaf yn defnyddio hynny pan fyddaf yn siarad â Thrysorlys y Deyrnas Unedig nesaf, pan wnaethoch chi ein hatgoffa ni i gyd fod gan gyrff llywodraethu ysgolion ac awdurdodau lleol fwy o bwerau cyllidol a phwerau benthyca na'r Senedd hon ei hun, o ran mynediad at gronfeydd wrth gefn yn benodol. Fe ddywedoch chi na ddylai Trysorlys y Deyrnas Unedig fod yn mân-reoli cyllid Cymru, ac mae hynny'n beth pwysig iawn i ni eu cael nhw ei ddeall.

Felly, rydyn ni wedi creu consensws yma heddiw. Nid yw'n cynnwys Reform. Wnaf i ddim colli unrhyw gwsg dros hynny. Ond os caf i orffen trwy ddweud bod y cynigion hyn yn y cynnig hwn wedi'u gwreiddio mewn partneriaeth, tegwch ac uchelgais drawsbleidiol ar y cyd i wella canlyniadau i bobl Cymru. Ac os nad oedd hynny'n werth awr o amser y Senedd hon, yna dydw i ddim yn gwybod beth sydd.
